rashi.heb:
*וַיְהִי אַחֲרֵי מוֹת משֶׁה.* 
מְחוּבָּר עַל סֵדֶר הַתּוֹרָה הַמְסַיֶּימֶת בִּפְטִירַת משֶׁה, וְזֶה מְחוּבָּר לָהּ.
rashi.eng: *And it was after the death of Moses.* This is connected to the order of the Torah which ends with Moses’ passing, and this follows it.

notes.2: (tn, Heb): “this Jordan”; the word “River” has been supplied in the translation for clarity (likewise in v. 11).
notes.3: (tc, Heb): “Cross over this Jordan, you and all these people, to the land that I am giving to them, to the children of Israel.” The final phrase, “to the children of Israel,” is probably a later scribal addition specifying the identity of “these people/them.”

rashi.heb:
*משֶׁה עַבְדִּי מֵת.* 
וְאִילּוּ הָיָה קַיָּים, בּוֹ הָיִיתִי חָפֵץ. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דְּרָשׁוּהוּ (תמורה טז א) עַל שְׁלשֶׁת אֲלָפִים הֲלָכוֹת שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּכְּחוּ בִּימֵי אֶבְלוֹ שֶׁל משֶׁה. בָּא יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְשָׁאַל, אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּבָּ"ה: משֶׁה עַבְדִּי מֵת וְהַתּוֹרָה עַל שְׁמוֹ נִקְרֵאת, לוֹמַר לְךָ: אִי אֶפְשָׁר, צֵא וְטוֹרְדָן בְּמִלְחָמָה.
rashi.eng: *Moses My servant has died.* If he were alive, I would prefer him. The Rabbis interpret this passage as a reference, not to Moses the leader, but to Moses the Lawgiver, concerning the 3,000 laws that were forgotten during the period of mourning for Moses. Joshua came and asked the Lord to repeat these laws to him. Said to him the Holy One, Blessed be He: Moses My servant has died, and the Torah is called by his name, implying to you that it is impossible [to convey them to you.] Go out and occupy them with martial activities.

notes.4: (tn, Heb): “Every place on which the sole of your foot walks, to you I have given it, as I said to Moses.” The second person pronouns in vv. 3-4 are plural, indicating that all the people are addressed here. The verbal form נְתַתִּיו (n�tattiv, “I have given it”) is probably a perfect of certitude, emphasizing the certainty of the action. Another option is to translate, “I have already assigned it.” In this case the verb would probably refer to the Lord’s decree to Abraham that he would give this land to his descendants.

rashi.heb:
*כָּל מָקוֹם אֲשֶׁר תִּדְרֹךְ.* 
כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ נֶאֱמַר לְמשֶׁה, וְשָׁנִינוּ בְּסִפְרֵי (פר' עקב): אִם לְלַמֵּד עַל תְּחוּמֵי אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר: מֵהַמִּדְבָּר וְהַלְּבָנוֹן הַזֶּה, אִם כֵּן לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר: כָּל מָקוֹם אֲשֶׁר תִּדְרֹךְ כַּף אַף חוּצָה לָאָרֶץ, מִשֶּׁתִּכְבְּשׁוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ, כָּל מַה שֶּׁתִּכְבְּשׁוּ מִחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ יִהְיֶה קָדוֹשׁ וְיִהְיֶה שֶׁלָּכֶם.
rashi.eng: *Every place on which [the soles of your feet] will tread.* A similar statement to this was said to Moses, concerning which we learned in Sifrei : If this verse is to teach about the boundaries of Eretz Israel, the Scripture already states: From this desert and Lebanon etc., [clearly defining the boundaries of the Holy Land.] If so, why is it stated, ‘Every place where your foot will tread?’ Even outside of Eretz Israel. [I.e.] After you have conquered the land, all that you will conquer outside the land, will be holy and will be yours.

notes.5: (tn, Heb): “all the land of the Hittites.” The expression “the land of the Hittites” does not refer to Anatolia (modern Turkey), where the ancient Hittite kingdom of the second millennium b.c. was located, but rather to Syria, the “Hatti land” mentioned in inscriptions of the first millennium b.c. (see HALOT 1:363). The phrase is omitted in the LXX and may be a scribal addition.
notes.6: (tn, Heb): “the Great Sea,” the typical designation for the Mediterranean Sea.
notes.7: (tn, Heb): “From the wilderness and this Lebanon even to the great river, the River Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, even to the great sea [at] the place where the sun sets, your territory will be.”

rashi.heb:
*מֵהַמִּדְבָּר וְהַלְּבָנוֹן הַזֶּה.* 
הוּא מִדְבַּר קָדֵשׁ, מִדְבַּר צִין שֶׁעַל יְדֵי אֱדוֹם, שֶׁהָיָה בְּמִקְצוֹעַ דְּרוֹמִית מִזְרָחִית וְדֶרֶךְ שָׁם נִכְנְסוּ לָאָרֶץ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (במדבר כ טז): וְהִנֵּה אֲנַחְנוּ בְקָדֵשׁ וְגוֹמֵר, וּמִנַּיִין שֶׁהָיָה בִּדְּרוֹמִית מִזְרָחִית, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שם לד ג): וְהָיָה לָכֶם פְּאַת נֶגֶב מִמִּדְבַּר צִין עַל יְדֵי אֱדוֹם.
rashi.eng: *From this desert and Lebanon.* [I.e.] the Desert of Kadesh, the Desert of Zin [that is near Edom], which was in the southeastern corner, through which they entered the land, as it is stated: And behold, we are in Kadesh. Now, whence is it derived that it was in the southeast? For it is stated: And the south side shall be to you from the desert of Zin near Edom etc.

rashi.heb:
*וְעַד הַנָּהָר הַגָּדוֹל נְהַר פְּרָת.* 
זֶה רָחְבָּהּ מִדָּרוֹם לְצָפוֹן.
rashi.eng: *to the great river, the Euphrates.* This is its width from south to North.

rashi.heb:
*כָּל אֶרֶץ הַחִתִּים.* 
בַּכְּלָל הַזֶּה.
rashi.eng: *all the land of the Hittites.* is included.

rashi.heb:
*וְעַד הַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל מְבוֹא הַשָּׁמֶשׁ.* 
לְאָרְכָּהּ, מִן הַמִּזְרָח לַמַּעֲרָב.
rashi.eng: *to the great sea westward.* Lengthwise from east to west.

notes.8: (tn, Heb): “A man will not stand before you.” The second person pronouns in this verse are singular, indicating Joshua is the addressee.

notes.9: (tn, Heb): “For you will cause these people to inherit the land that I swore to their fathers to give to them.” The pronoun “them” at the end of the verse refers to either the people or to the fathers.

rashi.heb:
*חֲזַק וֶאֱמָץ.* 
בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, כְּמָה שֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר: כִּי אַתָּה תַּנְחִיל.
rashi.eng: *Be strong and have courage.* in worldly pursuits, as the Scripture states: “For you will cause this nation to inherit the land.”

notes.11: (tn, Heb): “so you can be careful to do.” The use of the infinitive לִשְׁמֹר (lishmor, “to keep”) after the imperatives suggests that strength and bravery will be necessary for obedience. Another option is to take the form לִשְׁמֹר as a vocative lamed (ל) with imperative (see Isa 38:20 for an example of this construction), which could be translated, “Indeed, be careful!”
notes.13: (tn, Heb): “be wise,” but the word can mean “be successful” by metonymy.

rashi.heb:
*רַק חֲזַק וֶאֱמַץ מְאֹד.* 
בְּתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר: לִשְׁמֹר וְלַעֲשׂוֹת כְּכָל הַתּוֹרָה.
rashi.eng: *Just be strong and very courageous.* in Torah, as the Scripture states: “To observe and to do in accordance with all of the Torah.”

rashi.heb:
*תַּשְׂכִּיל.* 
תַּצְלִיחַ.
rashi.eng: *succeed.* Heb. תשכיל: succeed.

notes.15: (tn, Heb): “mouth.” This law scroll must not leave your lips. The ancient practice of reading aloud to oneself as an aid to memorization is in view here.
notes.16: (tn, Heb): “read it in undertones,” or “recite it quietly” (see HALOT 1:237).
notes.18: (tn, Heb): “you will make your way prosperous.”
notes.19: (tn, Heb): “and be wise,” but the word can mean “be successful” by metonymy.

rashi.heb:
*סֵפֶר הַתּוֹרָה הַזֶּה.* 
סֵפֶר מִשְׁנֵה תּוֹרָה הָיָה לְפָנָיו.
rashi.eng: *This book of the Torah.* The book of Deuteronomy was before him.

rashi.heb:
*וְהָגִיתָ בּוֹ.* 
וְהִתְבּוֹנַנְתָּ בּוֹ, כָּל הִגָּיוֹן שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה בַּלֵּב, כְּמָה דְּאַתְּ אָמַר (תהלים יט טו): וְהֶגְיוֹן לִבִּי לְפָנֶיךָ, (ישעיהו לג יח): לִבְּךָ יֶהְגֶּה אֵימָה.
rashi.eng: *And you shall meditate therein.* והגית. Every expression of הגיון in the Scriptures refers to the heart, as it is stated: “And the meditation of my heart (והגיון לבי) before you.” Your heart will meditate (יהגה) fear.

notes.20: (tn, Heb): “Have I not commanded you?” The rhetorical question emphasizes the importance of the following command by reminding the listener that it is being repeated.

rashi.heb:
*הֲלוֹא צִוִּיתִיךָ חֲזַק וֶאֱמָץ.* 
בְּמִלְחָמָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: אַל תַּעֲרֹץ וְאַל תֵּחָת. וְהֵיכָן צִוָּהוּ בִּימֵי משֶׁה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים לא כג): וַיְצַו אֶת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן־נוּן וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *Did I not command you, be strong and have courage.* in war; as it is stated: Do not fear and not be dismayed. Now, when did he command him? In Moses’ time, as it is stated: “And command Joshua, etc.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיְצַו יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.* 
בְּיּוֹם שֶׁתַּמּוּ יְמֵי בְּכִי אֵבֶל משֶׁה.
rashi.eng: *And Joshua commanded.* on the day that the days of the weeping in the mourning of Moses were ended.

notes.24: (tn, Heb): “to enter to possess the land which the Lord your God is giving to you to possess it.”

rashi.heb:
*הָכִינוּ לָכֶם צֵדָה.* 
כָּל דָּבָר הַצָּרִיךְ לַדֶּרֶךְ וּכְלֵי זֵינָם לַמִּלְחָמָה אָמַר לָהֶם לְתַקֵּן, שֶׁאִם אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּמַאֲכָל וּבְמִשְׁתֶּה, הֲרֵי הָיוּ מִסְתַּפְּקִים בַּמָּן שֶׁבִּכְלֵיהֶם עַד ט"ז בְּנִיסָן, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר (לקמן ה יב): וַיִּשְׁבֹּת הַמָּן מִמָּחֳרָת (מִפִּי רַבִּי).
rashi.eng: *Prepare provisions for yourselves.* everything necessary for the way. He told them to prepare weapons for battle. For, if you say it refers to food and drink, were they not supplied by the manna which was in their vessels until Nissan 16? For so it is stated: “And the manna ceased on the morrow.”

rashi.heb:
*בְּעוֹד שְׁלשֶׁת יָמִים.* 
בְּסוֹף שְׁלשֶׁת יָמִים, בְּעוֹד שֶׁתִּהְיוּ כָּאן שְׁלשֶׁת יָמִים וְאַחַר תַּעֲבֹרוּ.
rashi.eng: *in another three days.* [lit. in yet three days, i.e.] At the end of three days, when you will still be here three days, and afterwards you will cross.

notes.25: (tn, Heb): “remember the word which Moses, the Lord’s servant, commanded you.” This command can be found in Deut 3:18-20. In vv. 13-15 Joshua paraphrases the command, as the third person reference to Moses in v. 14 indicates.
notes.26: (tn, Heb): “is providing rest for you and is giving to you this land.” “This land” refers to the trans-Jordanian lands allotted to these tribes.

notes.27: (tn, Heb): “But you must cross over armed for battle before your brothers, all [you] mighty men of strength.”

rashi.heb:
*כָּל גִּבּוֹרֵי הַחַיִל.* 
שֶׁבָּכֶם יַעַבְרוּ חֲלוּצִים.
rashi.eng: *all the warriors.* among you shall cross over armed.

notes.28: (tn, Heb): “Then you may return to the land of your possession and possess it, that which Moses, the Lord’s servant, gave to you beyond the Jordan toward the rising of the sun.”

rashi.heb:
*מִזְרַח הַשָּׁמֶשׁ.* 
עֵבֶר מִזְרָחִי שֶׁל יַרְדֵּן.
rashi.eng: *toward the rising of the sun.* The eastern side of the Jordan.

notes.30: (tn): Or “Only.” Here and in v. 18 this word qualifies what precedes (see also v. 7).

notes.31: (tn, Heb): “any man who rebels against your mouth and does not listen to your words, to all which you command us, will be put to death.”
notes.32: (tn): Or “Only.” Here and in v. 17 this word qualifies what precedes (see also v. 7).

rashi.heb:
*יַמְרֶה.* 
יַקְנִיט אֶת דְּבָרֶיךָ.
rashi.eng: *that shall rebel [against your words].* defy your words.

notes.33: (tn, Heb): “Joshua, son of Nun, sent from Shittim two men, spies, secretly, saying.”
notes.34: (tn, Heb): “go, see the land, and Jericho.” For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.
notes.35: (tn, Heb): “they went and entered the house of a woman, a prostitute, and her name was Rahab, and they slept there.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּשְׁלַח יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְגוֹ'.* 
עַל כָּרְחִי אֲנִי צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ יְמֵי אֵבֶל משֶׁה שְׁלָחָם, שֶׁהֲרֵי לְסוֹף ג' יָמִים שֶׁתַּמּוּ יְמֵי אֵבֶל משֶׁה עָבְרוּ אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן, שֶׁמִּשָּׁם אָנוּ לְמֵדִים שֶׁמֵּת משֶׁה בְּז' אֲדָר כְּשֶׁאַתָּה מוֹנֶה ל"ג לְמַפְרֵעַ מִיּוֹם שֶׁעָלוּ מִן הַיַּרְדֵּן בֶּעָשׂוֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן, וְעַל כָּרְחָךְ מִשֶּׁנִּשְׁתַּלְּחוּ הַמְרַגְּלִים לֹא עָבְרוּ אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן עַד יוֹם הַחֲמִישִׁי, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיֵּשְׁבוּ שָׁם שְׁלשֶׁת יָמִים עַד־שָׁבוּ הָרוֹדְפִים בּוֹ בַּלַּיְלָה, וַיַּעַבְרוּ וַיָּבֹאוּ אֶל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן־נוּן... וַיַּשְׁכֵּם יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּבֹּקֶר וַיִּסְעוּ מֵהַשִּׁטִּים הֲרֵי יוֹם ד', וַיָּלִינוּ שָׁם טֶרֶם יַעֲבֹרוּ נִמְצָא שֶׁלֹּא עָבְרוּ עַד יוֹם ה'.
rashi.eng: *And Joshua [the son of Nun] sent [two men out of Shittim to spy].* Against my will I must say that he dispatched them during Moses’ mourning period, for after three days following the termination of Moses’ mourning period, they crossed the Jordan, for thence we deduced that Moses died on Adar 7 by counting back thirty-three days from the day they came up from the Jordan, namely, the tenth day of the first month. Now, of necessity, from the time the spies were dispatched, they did not cross the Jordan until the fifth day, as it is stated: and stayed there three days until the pursuers returned. On that night they crossed over and came to Joshua the son of Nun, and Joshua rose up early in the morning, and they moved from Shittim, here is a fourth day. And they lodged there before they crossed over. Hence, they did not cross until the fifth day.

rashi.heb:
*חֶרֶשׁ.* 
בְּרָז, כָּךְ תִּירְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן, אָמַר לָהֶם: עֲשׂוּ עַצְמְכֶם כְּחֵרְשִׁים, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יַסְתִּירוּ דִּבְרֵיהֶם מִפְּנֵיכֶם. דָּבָר אַחֵר: חֶרֶשׁ חֶרֶס, הַטְעִינוּ עַצְמְכֶם קְדֵרוֹת כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּהְיוּ נִרְאִין כְּקַדָּרִין.
rashi.eng: *secretly.* Secretly. So did Jon. render it. He said to them: Disguise yourselves as deaf-mutes (חרשים) so that they will not conceal their affairs from you. Another explanation is: חרש [with a “shin”] is like חרש [with a “sin” or “samech,” namely pottery.] Load yourselves with pots so that you appear as potters.

rashi.heb:
*רְאוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ וְאֶת יְרִיחוֹ.* 
וַהֲלֹא יְרִיחוֹ בִּכְלָל הָיְתָה וְלָמָּה יָצָאת, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיְתָה קָשָׁה כְּנֶגֶד כּוּלָּם, לְפִי שֶׁהָיְתָה יוֹשֶׁבֶת עַל הַסְּפָר. וְכַיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ (שמואל ב ב ל): וַיִּפָּקְדוּ מֵעַבְדֵי דָּוִד תִּשְׁעָה־עָשָׂר אִישׁ וַעֲשָׂהאֵל, וַהֲלֹא עֲשָׂהאֵל בִּכְלָל הָיָה וְלָמָּה יָצָא, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיָה קָשֶׁה כְּנֶגֶד כּוּלָּם, כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ (מלכים א יא א): וְהַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה אָהַב נָשִׁים נָכְרִיּוֹת רַבּוֹת וְאֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה, וַהֲלֹא בַּת פַּרְעֹה בִּכְלָל הָיְתָה וְלָמָּה יָצָאת, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיָה מְחַבְּבָהּ כְּנֶגֶד כּוּלָּם, וּכְלַפֵּי חֵטְא שֶׁהֶחֱטִיאָה אוֹתוֹ יוֹתֵר מִכּוּלָּן, כָּךְ שְׁנוּיָיה בְּסִפְרֵי (עקב נב).
rashi.eng: *and see the land and Jericho.* Now, was Jericho not included in the generalization? Why, then, is it specifed? Because it was as strong as all of them [the cities combined], it was situated on the boundary. Similarly, and there were missing of David’s servants nineteen men and Asahel. Now, was Asahel not included in the generalization? Why, then, was he specified? Because he was as strong as all of them [combined]. Similarly, and King Solomon loved many foreign wives and Pharaoh’s daughter. Now, was Pharaoh’s daughter not included in the generalization? Why, then, was she specified? Because he loved her as much as all of them [combined]. And regarding the sin, since she caused him to sin more than all of them. This was taught in Sifrei.

rashi.heb:
*אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה.* 
תִּירְגֵּם יְהוֹנָתָן: פּוּנְדְּקִיתָא, מוֹכֶרֶת מִינֵי מְזוֹנוֹת.
rashi.eng: *Innkeeper.* זונה. Targum Jon. renders: Innkeeper, one who sells various foodstuffs (מזונות).

notes.37: (tn, Heb): “men have come here tonight from the sons of Israel.”

rashi.heb:
*לַחְפֹּר.* 
לְרַגֵּל, כְּמוֹ (איוב לט כט): מִשָּׁם חָפַר אֹכֶל.
rashi.eng: *to search.* לחפר [lit. to dig,] to spy. And similarly: Thence he sought (חפר) food.

notes.38: (tn, Heb): “and the king of Jericho sent to Rahab, saying.”
notes.40: (tn): The idiom “come to” (בוֹא אֶל, bo’ ’el) probably has sexual connotations here, as it often does elsewhere when a man “comes to” a woman. If so, the phrase could be translated “your clients.” The instructions reflect Rahab’s perspective as to the identity of the men.
notes.41: (tn, Heb): The words “the ones who came to your house” ( “who came to your house”) may be a euphemistic scribal addition designed to blur the sexual connotation of the preceding words.

notes.42: (tn, Heb): “The woman took the two men and hid him.” The third masculine singular pronominal suffix on “hid” has to be a scribal error (see GKC �135.p).
notes.43: (tn, Heb): “the men came to me.” See the note on this phrase in v. 3.

rashi.heb:
*וַתִּצְפְּנוֹ.* 
יֵשׁ מִקְרָאוֹת מְדַבְּרִים עַל הָרַבִּים כְּיָחִיד, לְפִי שֶׁמִּיהֲרָה בְּהַטְמָנָתָם וּבְמָקוֹם צַר, כְּאִילּוּ הָיָה יְחִידִי, וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדַת תַּנְחוּמָא יֵשׁ (שלח א): פִּנְחָס וְכָלֵב הָיוּ, וּפִנְחָס עָמַד לִפְנֵיהֶם וְלֹא רָאוּהוּ לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה כְּמַלְאָךְ. דָּבָר אַחֵר: וַתִּצְפְּנוֹ כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, וְדוּגְמָתוֹ מָצִינוּ (משלי כז ט): שֶׁמֶן וּקְטֹרֶת יְשַׂמַּח לֵב, וְלֹא אָמַר יְשַׂמְּחוּ לֵב.
rashi.eng: *and had hidden them.* [lit.“and had hidden him.”] Some Scriptural passages treat the plural as singular. [In this case,] because she hastened to hide them, and [she hid them] in a narrow place as though they were one man. The Agadic Midrash of Rabbi Tanhuma states: They were Phinehas and Caleb, and Phinehas stood before them, yet they did not see him because he was like an angel. Another explanation is: And she hid him, [i.e.,] each one by himself. And we have found the like thereof: Oil and incense make joyful the heart. (ישמח לב), sing. form.) And it is not written ישמחו לב (plural form), [implying that each one makes the heart joyful.]

notes.44: (tn, Heb): “And the gate was to be shut in the darkness and the men went out.”

rashi.heb:
*בְּפִשְׁתֵּי הָעֵץ.* 
פִּשְׁתִּים בְּגִבְעוֹלֵיהֶן.
rashi.eng: *with the stalks of flax.* With their capsules.

notes.46: (tn): Another way to translate vv. 6-7 would be, “While she took them up to the roof and hid them…, the king’s men tried to find them….” Both of the main clauses have the subject prior to the predicate, perhaps indicating simultaneous action. (On the grammatical point, see R. J. Williams, Hebrew Syntax, 42, �235.) In this case Rahab moves the Israelite spies from the hiding place referred to in v. 4 to a safer and less accessible hiding place.
notes.47: (tn): The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied for clarity.
notes.48: (tn, Heb): “And the men chased after them [on] the road [leading to] the Jordan to the fords.” The text is written from the perspective of the king’s men. As far as they were concerned, they were chasing the spies.
notes.49: (tn, Heb): “And they shut the gate after – as soon as the ones chasing after them went out.” The expressions “after” and “as soon as” may represent a conflation of alternate readings.

rashi.heb:
*עַל הַמַּעְבְּרוֹת.* 
מְקוֹם מַעֲבַר הַמַּיִם, שֶׁהָיוּ סְבוּרִים שֶׁחָזְרוּ לַאֲחוֹרֵיהֶם אֶל עַרְבוֹת מוֹאָב, וְהַיַּרְדֵּן מַפְסִיק בֵּינְתַיִם.
rashi.eng: *to the fords.* the place for crossing the water, for they thought that they had turned back towards the Plains of Moab, and the Jordan stood in between.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַשַּׁעַר סָגָרוּ.* 
הַשּׁוֹעֲרִים.
rashi.eng: *they shut the gate.* [I.e.,] the gatekeepers.

notes.51: (tn, Heb): “she”; the referent (Rahab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.52: (tn): The Hebrew text adds, “to them.” This is somewhat redundant in English and has not been translated.

notes.53: (tn, Heb): “has given the land to you.” Rahab’s statement uses the Hebrew perfect, suggesting certitude.
notes.54: (tn, Heb): “terror of you has fallen upon us.”
notes.56: (tn): Both of these statements are actually subordinated to “I know” in the Hebrew text, which reads, “I know that the Lord…and that terror of you…and that all the inhabitants….”

notes.57: (tn, Heb): “and what you did to the two Amorite kings who were beyond the Jordan, Sihon and Og, how you annihilated them.”

notes.58: (tn, Heb): “And we heard and our heart[s] melted and there remained no longer breath in a man because of you.”

rashi.heb:
*וְלֹא קָמָה עוֹד רוּחַ בְּאִישׁ.* 
אֲפִילּוּ לִּשְׁכַּב עִם אִשָּׁה, אָמְרוּ: אֵין לְךָ כָּל שַׂר וְנָגִיד שֶׁלֹּא בָּא אֶל רָחָב הַזּוֹנָה, וּבַת עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים הָיְתָה כְּשֶׁיָּצְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרַיִם, וְזִנְּתָה כָּל אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה (זבחים קטז ב).
rashi.eng: *nor did there remain (or arise) anymore spirit.* And there did not remain anymore spirit, even to lie with a woman. [This was evident to Rahab] because, as the Rabbis said: There was neither prince or ruler who had no relations with Rahab the harlot. She was ten years old when the Israelites departed from Egypt, and she practiced harlotry for forty years.

notes.59: (tn, Heb): “Now, swear to me by the Lord.” To swear an oath in the Lord’s name would make the Lord the witness and guarantor of the promise attached to the oath. If the person making the oath should go back on the promise, the Lord would judge him for breaking the contract.
notes.60: (tn, Heb): “with the house of my father.”
notes.61: (tn, Heb): “true sign,” that is, “an inviolable token or pledge.”

rashi.heb:
*אוֹת אֱמֶת.* 
שֶׁתַּעֲשׂוּ כְּשֶׁתָּבֹאוּ וַתִּכְבְּשׁוּ אֶת הָעִיר, שֶׁתַּכִּירוּ הָאוֹת וְתַחְיוּנִי.
rashi.eng: *a true token.* That you will make, so that when you come and conquer the city, that you will recognize the sign and let me live.

notes.63: (tn): The second person pronoun is masculine plural, indicating that Rahab’s entire family is in view.
notes.64: (tn, Heb): “Our lives in return for you to die.” If the lives of Rahab’s family are not spared, then the spies will pay for the broken vow with their own lives.
notes.65: (tn, Heb): “If you do not report this matter of ours.”
notes.66: (tn, Heb): “allegiance and faithfulness.” These virtual synonyms are joined in the translation as “unswerving allegiance” to emphasize the degree of promised loyalty.
notes.67: (tn): The second person pronoun is feminine singular, referring specifically to Rahab.

notes.68: (tn, Heb): “she”; the referent (Rahab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.69: (tc): The phrase “by a rope” is omitted in the LXX. It may be a later clarifying addition. If original, the omission in the LXX is likely due to an error of homoioarcton. A scribe’s or translator’s eye could have jumped from the initial ב (bet) in the phrase בַּחֶבֶל (bakhevel, “with a rope”) to the initial ב on the immediately following בְּעַד (b�’ad, “through”) and accidentally omitted the intervening letters.
notes.71: (tc): These explanatory statements are omitted in the LXX and probably represent a later scribal addition.

rashi.heb:
*וַתּוֹרִדֵם בַּחֶבֶל בְּעַד הַחַלּוֹן.* 
בְּאוֹתוֹ חֶבֶל וְחַלּוֹן הָיוּ הַנּוֹאֲפִים עוֹלִין אֵלֶיהָ. אָמְרָה: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, בְּאֵלּוּ חָטָאתִי בְּאֵלּוּ תִּמְחוֹל לִי.
rashi.eng: *And she let them down by a rope through the window.* [lit., by] the [rope.] By this very rope and window the sinners would ascend to her. She said: “O Lord of the universe! With these I have sinned. With these forgive me.”

notes.73: (tn, Heb): “so that the pursuers might not meet you.”
notes.74: (tn, Heb): “the pursuers.” The object (“you”) is not in the Hebrew text but is implied.

rashi.heb:
*עַד שׁוֹב הָרֹדְפִים.* 
רָאֲתָה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁיָּשׁוּבוּ לְסוֹף שְׁלשֶׁת יָמִים.
rashi.eng: *until the pursuers return.* There sprouted in Rahab an expression of Divine Spirit that they would return at the end of three days.

notes.75: (tn, Heb): “We are free from this oath of yours which you made us swear.” The words “unless the following conditions are met” are not in the Hebrew text, but are added for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*נְקִיִּים אֲנַחְנוּ.* 
הֲרֵי אָנוּ תּוֹלִין הַדָּבָר בָּךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת הָאוֹת הַזֶּה.
rashi.eng: *We will be blameless.* We are making this matter dependent upon you to make this sign.

notes.76: (tn, Heb): “Look! We are about to enter the land.”
notes.77: (tn, Heb): “the cord of this red thread.”
notes.78: (tn, Heb): “and your father and your mother and your brothers and all the house of your father gather to yourself to the house.”

rashi.heb:
*אֶת תִּקְוַת.* 
לְשׁוֹן קַו וְחֶבֶל.
rashi.eng: *line of scarlet thread.* תקות - an expression of a line (קו) or rope.

notes.79: (tn, Heb): “Anyone who goes out from the doors of your house to the outside, his blood is on his head. We are innocent.”
notes.80: (tn, Heb): “But anyone who is with you in the house, his blood is on our head if a hand should be on him.”

rashi.heb:
*דָּמוֹ בְרֹאשׁוֹ.* 
עֲוֹן הֲרִיגָתוֹ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ תְּהֵא, כִּי הוּא יִגְרוֹם מִיתָתוֹ.*
rashi.eng: *his blood shall be upon his head.* The guilt of his slaying will be upon his own head, for he will have caused his own death.

rashi.heb:
*דָּמוֹ בְרֹאשֵׁנוּ.* 
עֲוֹן הֲרִיגָתוֹ תְּהֵא עָלֵינוּ.
rashi.eng: *his blood shall be upon our head.* The guilt of his slaying will be upon us.

notes.81: (tn, Heb): “and if you report this matter of ours.”

notes.82: (tn, Heb): “According to your words, so it [will be].”
notes.83: (tn, Heb): “she sent them away and they went.”

notes.85: (tn, Heb): “the pursuers.” The object (“them”) is added for clarification.
notes.86: (tn, Heb): “the ones chasing them.” This has been rendered as “their pursuers” in the translation to avoid redundancy with the preceding clause.
notes.87: (tn, Heb): “The pursuers looked in all the way and did not find [them].”

notes.88: (tn): The words “the river,” though not in the Hebrew text, are added for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּעַבְרוּ.* 
אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן.
rashi.eng: *and crossed over.* the Jordan.

notes.89: (tn, Heb): “Surely the Lord has given into our hand all the land.” The report by the spies uses the Hebrew perfect, suggesting certitude.
notes.90: (tn, Heb): “are melting away because of us.”

notes.91: (tn, Heb): “And Joshua arose early in the morning and he and the Israelites left Shittim and came to the Jordan.”
notes.92: (tn): The words “the river,” though not in the Hebrew text, have been supplied in the translation for clarity.

notes.93: (sn): The ark of the covenant refers to the wooden chest that symbolized God’s presence among his covenant people.

rashi.heb:
*וַהֲלַכְתֶּם אַחֲרָיו.* 
נִשְׁתַּנָּה הַמַּסָּע הַזֶּה מִשְּׁאָר מַסָּעוֹת, שֶׁכָּל זְמָן שֶׁמֹּשֶׁה הָיָה קַיָּים הָיָה עַמּוּד הֶעָנָן נוֹסֵעַ תְּחִלָּה, וּמַרְאֶה לָהֶם הַדֶּרֶךְ וְהָאָרוֹן נוֹסֵעַ אַחַר ב' דְּגָלִים, עַכְשָׁיו הָאָרוֹן נוֹסֵעַ תְּחִלָּה.
rashi.eng: *and go after it.* This journey differs from other journeys, for whereas previously, in the days of Moses, the pillar of cloud would lead the way, the Ark following in the very middle of the camp after two divisions, [comprising the first six tribes, had passed], now the Ark would travel ahead.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַכֹּהֲנִים הַלְוִיִּם.* 
לְפִי שֶׁיָּצְאוּ כּוּלָּם מִלֵּוִי (אֲבִי) אֲבִי עַמְרָם נִקְרְאוּ לְוִיּם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁפֵּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה: בְּמ"ח מְקוֹמוֹת נִקְרְאוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים לְוִיּם. וְזֶה טַעְמוֹ שֶׁל דָּבָר (מפּי רבּי).
rashi.eng: *and the priests the Levites.* [This is explained in inverted order.] Since they are all descended from Levi, Amram’s grandfather, they are called Levites, as our Sages explain in Gen. Rabbah.: in forty-eight places, the priests were called Levites, this being the reason for it.

notes.96: (tn, Heb): “But there should be a distance between you and it, about two thousand cubits in measurement.” The precise distance is uncertain, but the measurement designated אַמָּה (’ammah, “cubit”) was probably equivalent to approximately eighteen inches (one and one-half feet, or 45 cm) in length.

rashi.heb:
*אַךְ רָחוֹק יִהְיֶה.* 
כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם הוּא.
rashi.eng: *But there shall be a distance.* This is respect for the Omnipresent.

rashi.heb:
*וּבֵינָיו.* 
כְּמוֹ וּבֵינוֹ, וְדוֹמֶה לוֹ (תהלים קמט ב): יִשְׂמַח יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעוֹשָׂיו. דָּבָר אַחֵר: ב' אֲרוֹנוֹת הָיוּ, שֶׁל שְׁכִינָה וְשֶׁל יוֹסֵף מְהַלְּכִין יַחַד.
rashi.eng: *between (you and) it.* The same as ובינו and between it, and similar to this: “Let Israel rejoice in his Maker” (בעשיו). Another explanation is: And between them, referring to the Holy Ark and the ark of Joseph’s remains, which were traveling together.

rashi.heb:
*כְּאַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה.* 
כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּהְיוּ יְכוֹלִין לֵילֵךְ וּלְהִתְפַּלֵּל לְפָנָיו בְּשַׁבָּת, כָּךְ מְפוֹרָשׁ בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא, לְפִי שֶׁיָּדַע שֶׁעֲתִידִין לִהְיוֹת צָרִים לִפְנֵי יְרִיחוֹ בַּשַּׁבָּת.
rashi.eng: *just two thousand cubits.* so that you be permitted to go and pray before it on the Sabbath. Thus it is explained in M.T. for he knew that they would besiege Jericho on the Sabbath.

rashi.heb:
*לְמַעַן אֲשֶׁר תֵּדְעוּ.* 
מוּסָב עַל: וַהֲלַכְתֶּם אַחֲרָיו.
rashi.eng: *that you may know.* This is connected with, “And go after it.”

rashi.heb:
*כִּי לֹא עֲבַרְתֶּם בַּדֶּרֶךְ.* 
לֹא הֲלַכְתֶּם בְּעִנְיָן זֶה עַד הֵנָּה.
rashi.eng: *for you have not passed this way before.* You have not gone in this manner until now.

rashi.heb:
*וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.* 
בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי, וְיוֹם ל' שֶׁל אֵבֶל הָיָה רִאשׁוֹן לְג' הַיָּמִים.
rashi.eng: *And Joshua said.* On the third day. And the thirtieth day of Moses’ mourning period was the first of the three days.

rashi.heb:
*הִתְקַדָּשׁוּ.* 
הִזְדַּמְּנוּ.
rashi.eng: *Prepare yourselves.* Prepare yourselves.

rashi.heb:
*כִּי מָחָר.* 
בְּעָבְרְכֶם אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן.
rashi.eng: *for tomorrow.* when you cross the Jordan.

rashi.heb:
*נִפְלָאוֹת.* 
תִּירְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: פְּרִישָׁן.
rashi.eng: *wonders.* Jonathan renders: wonders.

rashi.heb:
*וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים.* 
בְּיוֹם הַמָּחֳרָת.
rashi.eng: *And Joshua said to the priests.* on the morrow.

rashi.heb:
*שְׂאוּ אֶת אֲרוֹן הַבְּרִית.* 
עַד עַכְשָׁיו נָשְׂאוּ הַלְוִיִּם, וְהַיּוֹם הַכֹּהֲנִים.
rashi.eng: *Carry the Ark of the Covenant.* Until now the Levites carried it, but today the Priests.

notes.99: (tn): Or more literally, “to exalt you in the eyes of all Israel.”

notes.100: (tn, Heb): “the edge of the waters of the Jordan.” The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied for clarity.
notes.101: (tn, Heb): “stand in the Jordan.” Here the repetition of the word “Jordan” would be redundant according to contemporary English style, so it was not included in the translation.

rashi.heb:
*כְּבֹאֲכֶם עַד קְצֵה מֵי הַיַּרְדֵּן.* 
כְּשֶׁתִּכַּנְסוּ לִפְנִים מִשְּׂפָתוֹ.
rashi.eng: *When you come to the edge of the waters of the Jordan.* when you enter within its edge.

rashi.heb:
*בַּיַּרְדֵּן תַּעֲמֹדוּ.* 
עַד אֲשֶׁר יַעַבְרוּ כָּל הָעָם אֶל הָעֵבֶר הַשֵּׁנִי.
rashi.eng: *you shall stand still in the Jordan.* until all the people cross to the other side.

rashi.heb:
*גְּשׁוּ הֵנָּה.* 
צִמְצֵם אֶת כּוּלָּם בֵּין שְׁנֵי בַּדֵּי אָרוֹן, זֶה אֶחָד מִן הַמְּקוֹמוֹת שֶׁהֶחֱזִיק מוּעָט אֶת הַמְרוּבֶּה.
rashi.eng: *Come here.* He confined them all between the two staves of the Holy Ark. This is one of the instances wherein a small space contained a large quantity.

rashi.heb:
*בְּזֹאת תֵּדְעוּן.* 
בְּמַה שֶּׁאַתֶּם רוֹאִים שֶׁכֻּלְּכֶם מְצוּמְצָמִין כָּאן.
rashi.eng: *By this you shall know.* Since you see that all of you are confined here.

rashi.heb:
*הַבְּרִית אֲדוֹן כָּל הָאָרֶץ.* 
בְּרִית שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, שֶׁהוּא אֲדוֹן כָּל הָאָרֶץ. וְאַל תִּתְמַהּ עַל הַהֵ"א שֶׁל הַבְּרִית, שֶׁהַרְבֵּה מִקְרָאוֹת מְדַבְּרִים כָּךְ, כְּמוֹ: (מלכים ב טז יז) הַמִּסְגְּרוֹת הַמְּכוֹנֹת: (ירמיהו לא לט) הָעֵמֶק הַפְּגָרִים.
rashi.eng: *the covenant of the Lord of all the earth.* The covenant of the Holy One, Blessed be He, Who is the Lord of all the earth. Now, do not wonder about the ‘he’ of הברית [the covenant which should read ארון ברית] for many Scriptural passages are worded in this manner, such as המסגרות המכונות the borders of the bases, and העמק הפגרים the valley of the corpses.

rashi.heb:
*עֹבֵר לִפְנֵיכֶם.* 
מַקְדִּים לִפְנֵיכֶם לִיכָּנֵס לְתוֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּן.
rashi.eng: *is crossing ahead of you.* [עובר is interpreted in the sense of] preceding you to enter into the Jordan.

rashi.heb:
*קְחוּ לָכֶם שְׁנֵי עָשָׂר אִישׁ.* 
הָכִינוּ אוֹתָם לִהְיוֹת נְכוֹנִים לְמַה שֶּׁאֲצַוֶּה אוֹתָם כְּשֶׁתַּעַבְרוּ אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן.
rashi.eng: *take for yourselves twelve men.* Prepare them to be ready for that which I shall command them when you will cross the Jordan.

notes.107: (tn, Heb): “the waters of the Jordan, the waters descending from above, will be cut off so that they will stand in one pile.”

rashi.heb:
*הַמַּיִם הַיֹּרְדִים מִלְמָעְלָה.* 
לְמַטָּה, כְּדֶרֶךְ כָּל הַנְּהָרוֹת הַמּוֹשְׁכִים.
rashi.eng: *the waters that come down from above.* downstream, as is the manner of all flowing rivers.

rashi.heb:
*וְיַעַמְדוּ נֵד אֶחָד.* 
כְּשֶׁיֵּרְדוּ הַמַּיִם עַד מָקוֹם שֶׁנִּכְרְתוּ שָׁם וְאֵינָם יוֹרְדִים מִשָּׁם וּלְמַטָּה, אֶלָּא הֵם מִתְקַבְּצִים וְנִגְדָּשִׁין וְעוֹלִין לְמַעְלָה, כִּיפִּין עַל גַּבֵּי כִּיפִּין.
rashi.eng: *shall stand in one heap.* When the water flows downstream to the place where it will be cut off, it will not flow down farther, but will be gathered and heaped and will ascend to form stacks upon stacks.

rashi.heb:
*נֵד.* 
כְּמוֹ (תהלים לג ז): כּוֹנֵס כַּנֵּד: (ישעיהו יז יא), נֵד קָצִיר, לְשׁוֹן גּוֹבַהּ, וְכֵן חִבְּרָם מְנַחֵם.*
rashi.eng: *heap.* נד, Like: He gathers like a heap (כנד), A heap of harvest (נד), an expression of height. In this manner Menahem (the grammarian) joined them together.

notes.108: (tn): The verb, though not in the Hebrew, is added for clarification.

notes.110: (tn, Heb): “and the Jordan overflows all its banks all the days of harvest.” The lengthy description of the priests’ arrival at the Jordan and the parenthetical reminder that the Jordan was at flood stage delay the climax of the story and add to its dramatic buildup.

rashi.heb:
*גְּדוֹתָיו.* 
לְשׁוֹן שָׂפָה גְּבֹהָה.
rashi.eng: *its banks.* גדותיו, an expression of a high bank.

rashi.heb:
*כָּל יְמֵי קָצִיר.* 
שֶׁיְּמֵי נִיסָן יְמֵי קָצִיר הֵם.
rashi.eng: *all the time of harvest.* for the days of Nissan are the harvest season.

notes.111: (tn, Heb): “the waters descending from above stood still.”
notes.112: (tn, Heb): “they stood in one pile very far away.”
notes.113: (tn, Heb): “the [waters] descending toward the sea of the Arabah (the Salt Sea) were completely cut off.” The Salt Sea is an ancient name for the Dead Sea.
notes.114: (map): For the location of Jericho see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

rashi.heb:
*הַרְחֵק מְאֹד.* 
מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁעָמְדוּ שָׁם נִפְסְקוּ.
rashi.eng: *very far.* From the place where they [the Israelites] stood, they [the waters] were cut off.

rashi.heb:
*מֵאָדָם הָעִיר.* 
כָּךְ שְׁמָהּ.
rashi.eng: *from Adam the city.* So was its name.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַיֹּרְדִים.* 
אוֹתָם שֶׁהָיוּ יוֹרְדִים מִשָּׁם וּלְמַטָּה תְּחִלָּה.
rashi.eng: *and those that descended.* Those that had previonsly flowed downstream from there.

rashi.heb:
*תַּמּוּ נִכְרָתוּ.* 
עָבְרוּ כְּדֶרֶךְ הֲלִיכָתָן כְּכָל הַנְּחָלִים הַהוֹלְכִים אֶל הַיָּם עַד אֲשֶׁר תַּמּוּ.
rashi.eng: *were completely cut off.* They flowed on their course like all streams that flow into the sea, until they were completed.

notes.115: (tn, Heb): “and all Israel was crossing over on dry ground until all the nation had finished crossing the Jordan.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּעַמְדוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים.* 
אֵצֶל שְׂפַת הַיַּרְדֵּן.
rashi.eng: *and the priests.* stood by the bank of the Jordan.

rashi.heb:
*בְּתוֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּן.* 
וְכָל זְמָן שֶׁעָמְדוּ לֹא יָרְדוּ הַמַּיִם הָעֶלְיוֹנִים לְמַטָּה, וּבְתוֹךְ כָּךְ כָּל הָעָם עוֹבְרִים בְּחָרָבָה.
rashi.eng: *in the midst of the Jordan.* and as long as they stood, the upper waters did not flow downstream, and during this time, all the people were crossing on the dry ground.

rashi.heb:
*הָכֵן.* 
מְכוּוָּנִים וְנִצָּבִים זֶה כְּנֶגֶד זֶה.
rashi.eng: *firm arranged.* standing precisely opposite one another.

notes.116: (tn, Heb): “And when all the nation had finished crossing the Jordan.”

rashi.heb:
*שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר אֲנָשִׁים.* 
הֵם שֶׁנִּזְכָּרִים לְמַעְלָה לִהְיוֹת נְכוֹנִים.
rashi.eng: *twelve men.* They are the aforementioned, who were to be prepared.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַעֲבַרְתֶּם אוֹתָם עִמָּכֶם.* 
כְּמִצְוַת משֶׁה (דברים כז ד) לִבְנוֹת לָהֶם מִזְבֵּחַ בְּהַר עֵיבָל וְלִכְתּוֹב עֲלֵיהֶם אֶת דִּבְרֵי הַתּוֹרָה, וּבוֹ בַּיּוֹם בָּאוּ אֶל הַר עֵיבָל וּבָנוּ בָּהֶם אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְהֶעֱלוּ עוֹלוֹת וּשְׁלָמִים, וְאָכְלוּ וְשָׁתוּ, וְקִפְּלוּ אוֹתָם וּבָאוּ וְלָנוּ בַּגִּלְגָּל.
rashi.eng: *and you shall carry them over with you.* in accordance with Moses’ commandment to build an altar there with on Mt. Ebal and to write upon them the words of the Torah. On that very day, they came to Mt. Ebal, built therewith the altar, and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings, and they ate and drank and peeled them and came and lodged in Gilgal.

rashi.heb:
*עִבְרוּ לִפְנֵי אֲרוֹן וְגוֹ'.* 
הִכָּנְסוּ עַתָּה בַּיַּרְדֵּן וְעִבְרוּ עַד לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים.
rashi.eng: *Pass before the Ark etc..* Enter now into the Jordan and pass until you are in front of the priests.

notes.118: (tn, Heb): “that this may be”; the referent of “this” (the twelve stones) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.119: (tn, Heb): “in order that this might be a sign among you.”

notes.121: (tn, Heb): “how the waters descending from above stood still.”

rashi.heb:
*וְהָיוּ הָאֲבָנִים הָאֵלֶּה.* 
בַּגִּלְגָּל לְזִכְרוֹן זֶה.
rashi.eng: *and these stones shall be.* in Gilgal as a memorial of this.

notes.122: (tn): Here “also” has been supplied in the translation to make it clear (as indicated by v. 20) that these are not the same stones the men took from the river bed.

rashi.heb:
*וּשְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה אֲבָנִים.* 
אֲחֵרוֹת הֵקִים יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּתוֹךְ הַיַּרְדֵּן.
rashi.eng: *And twelve stones.* I.e. others Joshua set up in the midst of the Jordan.

rashi.heb:
*עַד תֹּם כָּל־הַדָּבָר.* 
כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ בְּמַסֶּכֶת סוֹטָה (לד א): עוֹדָם בַּיַּרְדֵּן, אָמַר לָהֶם יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: דְּעוּ לָמָּה אַתֶּם עוֹבְרִים אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן, עַל מְנָת שֶׁתּוֹרִישׁוּ אֶת כָּל יוֹשְׁבֵי הָאָרֶץ וְכוּ'.
rashi.eng: *until everything was finished.* as we learned in Tractate Sotah While they were still standing in the river bed of the Jordan, Joshua said to them: Know for what purpose you are crossing the Jordan. On the condition that you drive out all the inhabitants of the land etc.

notes.123: (tn, Heb): “in the presence of the people.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיְהִי כַּאֲשֶׁר תַּם כָּל הָעָם לַעֲבוֹר וַיַּעֲבֹר אֲרוֹן וְגוֹ'.* 
לֹא כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁעָבְרוּ הָאֲחֵרִים, אֶלָּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּפוֹרָשׁ לְמַטָּה בָּעִנְיָן (להלן פסוק יח): נִתְּקוּ כַּפּוֹת רַגְלֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים לַאֲחוֹרֵיהֶם אֶל הֶחָרָבָה עַל הַשָּׂפָה שֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ בָּהּ, שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹמְדִים אֶצְלָהּ, וְחָזְרוּ הַמַּיִם לַאֲחוֹרֵיהֶם לֵילֵךְ כִּתְמוֹל שִׁלְשׁוֹם; נִמְצָא, אֲרוֹן וְנוֹשְׂאָיו מִצַּד זֶה וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד זֶה, נָשָׂא הָאֲרוֹן אֶת נוֹשְׂאָיו וְעָבַר.
rashi.eng: *And it was, when all the people had completely passed over, that the Ark passed over, etc..* not after the manner in which the others had passed over, but as it is explained below in this episode, the soles of the priests’ feet were lifted up backwards to the dry land on the bank from which they had entered, beside which they were standing, and the waters returned backwards to flow as it had done heretofore. Hence, the Ark and its bearers are found to be on one side, and all Israel on the other side. The Ark picked up its bearers and passed over.

rashi.heb:
*לִפְנֵי הָעָם.* 
לְעֵינֵי הָעָם.
rashi.eng: *in the presence of the people.* [lit. before the people,] i.e. before the eyes of the people.

notes.126: (map): For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

notes.128: (tn, Heb): “all the days of his life.”

notes.130: (tn): Traditionally, “the ark of the testimony,” another name for the ark of the covenant. The Hebrew term עֵדוּת (’edut, “testimony” or “witness”) here refers to the Mosaic covenant and the body of stipulations contained within it (see HALOT 2:791).

rashi.heb:
*צַוֵּה אֶת הַכֹּהֲנִים.* 
כָּאן פֵּירַשׁ הַכָּתוּב אֶת הָאָמוּר לְמַעְלָה, הֵיאָךְ עָבַר אֲרוֹן ה' וְהַכֹּהֲנִים לִפְנֵי הָעָם וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *Command the priests.* Here the Scripture explains the aforementioned, how the Ark of the Lord and the priests passed over in the presence of the people etc.

rashi.heb:
*וְיַעֲלוּ מִן הַיַּרְדֵּן.* 
'וְיַעַבְרוּ' אֵין כְּתִיב כָּאן, אֶלָּא 'וְיַעֲלוּ', לָמַדְנוּ שֶׁעַל הַשָּׂפָה שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹמְדִין אֶצְלָהּ עָלוּ, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹמְדִין אֵצֶל שְׂפַת הַיַּרְדֵּן שֶׁבַּמַּעֲרָב, שֶׁהֲרֵי נֶאֱמַר לְמַעְלָה (ג טו) נִטְבְּלוּ רַגְלֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים בִּקְצֵה הַמַּיִם, וְשָׁם נֶאֱמַר וַיַּעַמְדוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹבְרִים.
rashi.eng: *that they come up out of the Jordan.* that they cross, is not written here, but “that they come up.” Hence, we deduce that they came up on the bank beside which they were standing. And it is impossible to say that they were standing beside the western bank of the Jordan, for it is stated above: The feet of the priests were dipped in the edge of the water. And there it is stated: And the priests stood and all Israel passed.

notes.131: (tn, Heb): “and the soles of the feet of the priests were brought up to the dry land.”
notes.132: (tn, Heb): “and the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and went as formerly over their banks.” Verses 15-18 give a more detailed account of the priests’ crossing that had been briefly described in v. 11.

rashi.heb:
*נִתְּקוּ כַּפּוֹת רַגְלֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים.* 
מִן הַמַּיִם אֶל הֶחָרָבָה שֶׁאֶצְלָם, וַיָּשׁוּבוּ הַמַּיִם לִמְקוֹמָם; נִמְצָא, אֲרוֹן מִצַּד זֶה וְיִשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד זֶה, נָשָׂא אֲרוֹן אֶת נוֹשְׂאָיו וְעָבַר. וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה נֶעֱנַשׁ עוּזָּא (שמואל ב ו ז) כְּשֶׁאָחַז בָּאָרוֹן, נוֹשְׂאָיו נָשָׂא, עַצְמוֹ לֹא כָּל שֶׁכֵּן.
rashi.eng: *the soles of the priests’ feet were lifted up.* from the water to the dry land which was beside them, and the waters returned to their place. Hence, the Ark is found to be on one side and Israel on the other side. Accordingly, the Ark lifted its bearers and passed over. And concerning this matter, Uzzah was punished when he took hold of the Ark. If it bore its bearers, can it not be deduced by a fortiori conclusion that it can bear itself?

notes.133: (sn): The first month was the month Abib (= late March-early April in the modern calendar). The Passover in Egypt also occurred on the tenth day of the first month (Exod 12:2; 13:4).
notes.134: (map): For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

notes.135: (tn, Heb): “these,” referring specifically to the twelve stones mentioned in vv. 3-7.

rashi.heb:
*הֵקִים יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּגִּלְגָּל.* 
הוּא הַמָּלוֹן אֲשֶׁר לָנוּ בּוֹ הַלַּיְלָה.
rashi.eng: *Joshua set up in Gilgal.* That is the lodging place where they lodged that night.

notes.138: (tn, Heb): “crossed this Jordan”; the word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied to clarify the meaning.

notes.139: (tn, Heb): “just as the Lord your God did to the Red Sea when he dried [it] up before us while we crossed over.”

notes.142: (tn, Heb): “know the hand of the Lord that it is strong.”

notes.144: (tc): Another textual tradition has, “while we crossed.”
notes.145: (tn, Heb): “their heart[s] melted and there was no longer in them breathe because of the sons of Israel.”

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן יָמָּה.* 
לְצַד שֶׁעָבְרוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, הוּא צַד שֶׁל מַעֲרָבִי, וְעַד עַכְשָׁיו הָיוּ בְּעֵבֶר מִזְרָחִי.
rashi.eng: *who were on the side of the Jordan westward.* on the side to which the children of Israel had crossed, i.e. the west side. And previously, they had been on the east side.

notes.146: (tn, Heb): “return, circumcise the sons of Israel a second time.” The Hebrew term שׁוּב (shuv, “return”) is used here in an adverbial sense to indicate the repetition of an action.

rashi.heb:
*חַרְבוֹת צֻרִים.* 
כְּתַּרְגּוּמוֹ: אִזְמְלָוָן חֲרִיפִין, וְכֵן (תהלים פט מד): אַף תָּשִׁיב צוּר חַרְבּוֹ, כְּשֶׁהַחֲרִיפוּת נֶהְפָּךְ לַצְּדָדִין וְאֵינוֹ חוֹתֵךְ יָפֶה, וְכֵן (ישעיהו נד יז): כָּל כְּלִי יוּצַר עָלַיִךְ.
rashi.eng: *sharp knives.* חרבות צרים, according to Targum, sharp knives, also “You have turned back the edge of his sword.” When the sharp edge is turned sideways and does not cut well. And so: “Every weapon which will be sharpened against you.”

rashi.heb:
*שֵׁנִית.* 
שֶׁמָּלוּ כְּבָר בְּלֵיל יְצִיאָתָם מִמִּצְרַיִם קָהָל גָּדוֹל יַחַד, וְזוֹ פַּעַם שֵׁנִית, שֶׁכָּל הָאַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה שֶׁהָיוּ בַּמִּדְבָּר לֹא נָשְׁבָה לָהֶם רוּחַ צְפוֹנִית וְלֹא הָיָה לָהֶם יוֹם נוֹחַ לָמוּל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (עא ב). וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ (שם): שֵׁנִית זוֹ פְּרִיעַת מִילָה שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ.
rashi.eng: *the second time.* for they had already circumcised a large assembly on the night of their departure from Egypt, and this was the second time, for the entire forty years that they were in the desert, the north wind did not blow for them, and they did not have any day suitable for circumcision, as we learned in Job. Our Rabbis state, however, “ ‘the second time’ refers the uncovering the corona at circumcision,” [i.e. splitting the membrane and pulling it back] which Abraham was not commanded to do.

notes.147: (tn): Or “Gibeath Haaraloth.” This name means “Hill of the Foreskins.” Many modern translations simply give the Hebrew name, although an explanatory note giving the meaning of the name is often included. The name given to the place, Hill of the Foreskins was an obvious reminder of this important event.

rashi.heb:
*גִּבְעַת הָעֲרָלוֹת.* 
עַל שֵׁם הַמְּאוֹרָע נִקְרָא, שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה כְּמִין גִּבְעָה.
rashi.eng: *the hill of the foreskins.* It was given this appellation to commemorate the event, because the foreskins were made into a sort of mound, or hillock.

notes.148: (tn, Heb): “All the people who went out from Egypt, the males, all the men of war, died in the desert in the way when they went out from Egypt.”

rashi.heb:
*וְזֶה הַדָּבָר.* 
עַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּר מָל אוֹתָם, אָמַר לָהֶם: סְבוּרִים אַתֶּם לִירַשׁ אֶת הָאָרֶץ עֲרֵלִים, לֹא כָּךְ נֶאֱמַר לְאַבְרָהָם (בראשית יז ט): וְאַתָּה אֶת־בְּרִיתִי תִשְׁמֹר וְגוֹמֵר (שם שם ח), וְנָתַתִּי לְךָ וּלְזַרְעֲךָ אַחֲרֶיךָ אֵת אֶרֶץ מְגֻרֶיךָ.
rashi.eng: *Now this is the reason.* Through speech he circumcised them. He said to them, “Do you expect to inherit the land while being uncircumcised? Was it not thus stated to Abraham: 'And you shall keep my covenant etc. And I shall give to you and to your seed after you the land of your sojournings?’ ”

rashi.heb:
*כָּל הָעָם הַיּוֹצֵא.* 
לֹא הָיָה אֶחָד מֵהֶם כָּאן, שֶׁכֻּלָּם מֵתוּ, וְהֵם הָיוּ מוּלִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: כִּי מֻלִים הָיוּ.
rashi.eng: *all the people that came out.* Not one of them was here, for they had all died, and they were circumcised, as it is stated: for… were circumcised.

rashi.heb:
*לֹא מָלוּ.* 
כְּמוֹ שֶׁפֵּירַשְׁתִּי, שֶׁלֹּא נָשְׁבָה רוּחַ צְפוֹנִית, וְהֵם שֶׁמָּלוּ עַכְשָׁיו.
rashi.eng: *they had not circumcised.* as I explained, that the north wind had not blown, and they were the ones who were circumcised now.

notes.152: (tn, Heb): “all the nation, the men of war who went out from Egypt, who did not listen to the voice of the Lord, came to an end.”
notes.153: (tn): Some Hebrew mss, as well as the Syriac version, support this reading. Most ancient witnesses read “us.”
notes.154: (tn, Heb): “flowing with.” The word picture a land rich in milk and honey depicts the land as containing many grazing areas (which would produce milk) and flowering plants (which would support the bees that produced honey).

notes.155: (tn, Heb): “their sons he raised up in their place.”

rashi.heb:
*וְאֶת בְּנֵיהֶם הֵקִים תַּחְתָּם.* 
וְאֶת בְּנֵיהֶם שֶׁהֵקִים תַּחְתֵּיהֶם, הֵם הַיִּלּוֹדִים בַּמִּדְבָּר, אוֹתָם מָל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
rashi.eng: *And their children whom he raised up in their stead.* i.e. And their children whom he raised up in their stead, (they are the ones who were born in the desert) them Joshua circumcised.

rashi.heb:
*וַיֵּשְׁבוּ תַּחְתָּם.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) בַּאֲתַרְהוֹן, וְלֹא צָרוּ עַל הָעִיר.
rashi.eng: *and they remained in their places.* in their places (Jonathan) and they did not besiege the city.

rashi.heb:
*עַד חֲיוֹתָם.* 
מִן הַמַּכָּה.
rashi.eng: *until they recovered.* from the wound.

notes.158: (sn): One might take the disgrace of Egypt as a reference to their uncircumcised condition (see Gen 34:14), but the generation that left Egypt was circumcised (see v. 5). It more likely refers to the disgrace they experienced in Egyptian slavery. When this new generation reached the promised land and renewed their covenantal commitment to the Lord by submitting to the rite of circumcision, the Lord’s deliverance of his people from slavery, which had begun with the plagues and the crossing of the Red Sea, reached its climax. See T. C. Butler, Joshua (WBC), 59.
notes.159: (sn): The name Gilgal sounds like the Hebrew verb “roll away” (גַּלַל, galal).

rashi.heb:
*גַּלּוֹתִי.* 
הֲסִירוֹתִי אֶת חֶרְפַּת מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים: רְאוּ כִּי רָעָה נֶגֶד פְּנֵיכֶם, כּוֹכָב אֶחָד יֵשׁ שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ 'רָעָה' וְהוּא סִימָן שֶׁל דָּם, רוֹאִין אָנוּ אוֹתוֹ עֲלֵיכֶם בַּמִּדְבָּר, וְהוּא שֶׁאָמַר משֶׁה בַּמִּדְבָּר (שמות לב יב): לָמָּה יֹאמְרוּ מִצְרַיִם לֵאמֹר בְּרָעָה הוֹצִיאָם, וְהֵם אֵינָם יוֹדְעִים שֶׁהוּא דַּם מִילָה, וּכְשֶׁמָּלוּ בִּימֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וּבָא אוֹתוֹ הַדָּם הוּסְרָה אוֹתָהּ הַחֶרְפָּה שֶׁעֲדַיִין עֵרֶב רַב שֶׁעָלוּ עִמָּהֶם הָיוּ מוֹנִים לָהֶם, כָּךְ דָרַשׁ רַבִּי משֶׁה הַדַּרְשָׁן.
rashi.eng: *have I rolled away.* I removed the reproach of the Egyptians who had said, “See that ‘Ra-ah’ is before your faces. There is a star named ‘Ra-ah’ which is a symbol of blood. We see it over you in the desert.” And that is what Moses said in the desert, “Why should the Egyptians say, With ‘Ra-ah’ He took them out.” But they did not know that that was the blood of circumcision. And when they circumcised in Joshua’s time, and that blood came, that reproach was removed, for the vast multitude which had gone up with them were still vexing them. In this manner, Rabbi Moses the preacher expounded.

rashi.heb:
*גַּלּוֹתִי.* 
הֲסִירוֹתִי, כְּמוֹ: (תהלים קיט כב), גַּל מֵעָלַי חֶרְפָּה: (בראשית כט י), וַיָּגֶל אֶת הָאֶבֶן.
rashi.eng: *have I rolled away.* גלותי - I have removed, like “(גל) Remove [or roll away] from me reproach and shame.” “ (ויגל) and he rolled off [or removed] the stone.”

notes.160: (map): For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

notes.161: (tn): The Hebrew text adds, “on this same day.” This is somewhat redundant in English and has not been translated.

rashi.heb:
*מִמָּחֳרַת הַפֶּסַח.* 
יוֹם הֲנָפַת הָעוֹמֶר, שֶׁהִקְרִיבוּ עוֹמֶר תְּחִלָּה וּמִז' בַּאֲדָר שֶׁמֵּת משֶׁה, שֶׁפָּסַק הַמָּן, הָיוּ מִסְתַפְּקִין עַד עַכְשָׁיו מִמָּן שֶׁבִּכְלֵיהֶם שֶׁלָּקְטוּ בְּשִׁבְעָה בַּאֲדָר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמות טז לה): אֶת הַמָּן אָכְלוּ אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה, וַהֲלֹא מ' שָׁנָה חָסֵר שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם, שֶׁהֲרֵי תְּחִלַּת יְרִידַת הַמָּן בְּט"ו בְּאִיָיר, אֱמוֹר מֵעַתָּה, בַּחֲרָרָה שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרַיִם טָעֲמוּ טַעַם מָן.
rashi.eng: *on the morrow of the Passover.* the day of the waving of the 'Omer, for first they sacrificed the 'Omer. And from the seventh of Adar, when Moses died, whereupon the manna ceased to fall, they subsisted on the manna which was in their vessels, which they had gathered on the seventh of Adar, as it is stated: “the manna they ate forty years.” Now, was it not forty years less thirty days, for the beginning of the falling of the manna was on the fifteenth of Iyar? Hence we deduce that in the cakes which the Israelites took with them from Egypt they perceived the taste of manna.

notes.162: (tn, Heb): “the day after, when they ate.” The present translation assumes this means the day after the Passover, though it is possible it refers to the day after they began eating the land’s produce.
notes.163: (tn, Heb): “and the sons of Israel had no more manna.”

rashi.heb:
*וְלֹא הָיָה עוֹד לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מָן.* 
לְפִיכָךְ: וַיֹּאכְלוּ מֵעֲבוּר הָאָרֶץ, אִם הָיָה לָהֶם מָן לֹא הָיוּ אוֹכְלִים מִן הַתְּבוּאָה, שֶׁהַמָּן הָיָה נוֹחַ לָהֶם, מָשָׁל אוֹמֵר לַתִּינוֹק: מִפְּנֵי מָה אַתָּה אוֹכֵל פַּת שְׂעוֹרִין, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין לִי פַּת חִטִּין, לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר: וְלֹא הָיָה עוֹד וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *neither had the children of Israel manna anymore.* Therefore, they ate of the grain of the Land. Had they still had manna, they would not have eaten of the grain, for the manna was pleasing to them. An appropriate parable is: One says to a child, why do you eat barley bread? Because he has no wheat bread. Therefore, it is stated: “Neither had the children of Israel manna anymore, etc.”

notes.165: (map): For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.
notes.166: (tn, Heb): “he lifted up his eyes and looked. And look, a man was standing in front of him, and his sword was drawn in his hand.” The verb הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”) invites the reader to view the scene through Joshua’s eyes. By calling the stranger “a man,” the author reflects Joshua’s perspective. The text shortly reveals his true identity (vv. 14-15).
notes.167: (tn, Heb): “Are you for us or for our enemies?”

rashi.heb:
*בִּהְיוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּירִיחוֹ.* 
מִכָּאן לְעִיבּוּרָהּ שֶׁל עִיר שֶׁהִיא מִן הָעִיר, שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר בְּתוֹךְ יְרִיחוֹ.*
rashi.eng: *when Joshua was in Jericho.* Hence we deduce that the outskirts of a city are considered as part of the city, for it is impossible to say [that he was actually] inside Jericho.

rashi.heb:
*הֲלָנוּ אַתָּה.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) הַלְמִסְעַדְנָא אֲתֵיתָא.
rashi.eng: *Are you for us.* Have you come to support us?

notes.168: (tc, Heb): “He said, “Neither.” An alternative reading is לוֹ (lo, “[He said] to him”; cf. NEB). This reading is supported by many Hebrew mss, as well as the LXX and Syriac versions. The traditional reading of the MT (לֹא, lo’, “no, neither”) is probably the product of aural confusion (the two variant readings sound the same in Hebrew). Although followed by a number of modern translations (cf. NIV, NRSV), this reading is problematic, for the commander of the Lord’s army would hardly have declared himself neutral.
notes.169: (sn): The Lord’s heavenly army, like an earthly army, has a commander who leads the troops. For the phrase שַׂר־צְבָא (sar-ts�va’, “army commander”) in the human sphere, see among many other references Gen 21:22, 32; 26:26; Judg 4:2, 7; 1 Sam 12:9.
notes.170: (sn): The commander’s appearance seems to be for Joshua’s encouragement. Joshua could now lead Israel into battle knowing that the Lord’s invisible army would ensure victory.
notes.171: (tn, Heb): “Joshua fell on his face to the ground and bowed down.”

rashi.heb:
*עַתָּה בָאתִי.* 
לְעֶזְרָתְךָ, שֶׁאֵין אָדָם יָכוֹל לְהִלָּחֵם עָלֶיהָ וּלְתוֹפְשָׂהּ לְהַפִּיל הַחוֹמָה, אֲבָל בִּימֵי משֶׁה רַבָּךְ בָּאתִי וְלֹא חָפֵץ בִּי, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שמות לג טו): אִם אֵין פָּנֶיךָ הֹלְכִים וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *I have now come.* to your aid, for no man can wage war against it [Jericho] and seize it, to throw down the wall. But in the time of Moses your master, I came and he did not want me, as it is stated: “if Your presence does not go, etc.”

rashi.heb:
*שַׂר צְבָא ה'.* 
יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהוּא צָבָא לַה', וּמִיכָאֵל הָיָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דניאל י כא): מִיכָאֵל שַׂרְכֶם.
rashi.eng: *the captain of the Lord’s host.* Israel, who is the Lord’s host. Now, this was Michael, as it is said: “Michael your prince.”

notes.172: (map): For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.
notes.173: (tn, Heb): “was shutting and shut up.” HALOT 2:743 paraphrases, “blocking [any way of access] and blocked [against any who would leave].”
notes.174: (tn, Heb): “there was no one going out and there was no one coming in.”

rashi.heb:
*סֹגֶרֶת וּמְסֻגֶּרֶת.* 
כְּתַּרְגּוּמוֹ: אֲחִידָא בְּדָשִׁין דְּפַרְזְלָא, וּמִתַּקְּפָא בְּעִבָּרִין דִּנְחָשׁ.
rashi.eng: *had shut its gates and was barred.* according to Targum , closed with iron gates and reinforced with copper bolts.

notes.175: (tn, Heb): “I have given into your hand Jericho.” The Hebrew verb נָתַתִּי (natatti, “I have given”) is probably best understood as a perfect of certitude, indicating the certainty of the action. The Hebrew pronominal suffix “your” is singular, being addressed to Joshua as the leader and representative of the nation. To convey to the modern reader what is about to happen and who is doing it, the translation “I am about to defeat Jericho for you” has been used.

notes.176: (tn, Heb): “and go around the city, all [you] men of war, encircling the city one time.” The Hebrew verb וְסַבֹּתֶם (v�sabbotem, “and go around”) is plural, being addressed to the whole army.

rashi.heb:
*הַיּוֹבְלִים.* 
אֵילִים.
rashi.eng: *rams’ horns.* Heb. הַיּוֹבְלִים.

notes.178: (tn): Heb “and it will be at the sounding of the horn, the ram’s horn, when you hear the sound of the ram’s horn.” The text of Josh 6:5 seems to be unduly repetitive, so for the sake of English style and readability, it is best to streamline the text here. The reading in the Hebrew looks like a conflation of variant readings, with the second (“when you hear the sound of the ram’s horn”) being an interpolation that assimilates the text to verse 20 (“when the army heard the sound of the horn”). Note that the words “when you hear the sound of the ram's horn” do not appear in the LXX of verse 5.
notes.179: (tn, Heb): “all the people will shout with a loud shout.”
notes.181: (tn, Heb): “and the people will go up, each man straight ahead.”

rashi.heb:
*בִּמְשֹׁךְ.* 
בִּתְקִיעָה אַחֲרוֹנָה, בְּהַאֲרִיךְ הַתּוֹקֵעַ אֶת הַקּוֹל.
rashi.eng: *a long blast.* with the final blast, when the blower lengthens the note.

rashi.heb:
*תַּחְתֶּיהָ.* 
בִּמְקוֹמָהּ.
rashi.eng: *in its place.* Heb. תַּחְתֶּיהָ [lit.,] under it.

notes.182: (tn): An alternative reading is “and they said.” In this case the subject is indefinite and the verb should be translated as passive, “[the army] was told.”

notes.185: (tn, Heb): “when Joshua spoke to the people.”

rashi.heb:
*וְהֶחָלוּץ.* 
בְּנֵי רְאוּבֵן וּבְנֵי גָד הָיוּ עוֹבְרִים לִפְנֵיהֶם, לְפִי שֶׁהָיוּ בְּנֵי גָד גִּבּוֹרִים וּמַכִּים בִּזְרוֹעַ חֲזָקָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים לג כ): וְטָרַף זְרוֹעַ אַף קָדְקֹד.
rashi.eng: *And the armed ones.* The children of Reuben and the children of Gad were passing before them, because the children of Gad were mighty warriors and would strike with a strong arm, as it is said: “And he tears the arms, even the crown of the head.”

notes.188: (tn, Heb): “do not let a word come out of your mouths.”

notes.191: (tn, Heb): “and he made the ark of the Lord go around the city, encircling one time.”
notes.192: (tn, Heb): “and they entered the camp and spent the night in the camp.”

notes.193: (tn, Heb): “Joshua rose early in the morning and the priests picked up the ark of the Lord.”

rashi.heb:
*וְהַמְאַסֵּף.* 
שֵׁבֶט דָּן הַנּוֹסֵעַ אַחֲרוֹן, וְהוּא מְאַסֵּף אֶת כָּל הַמִּתְעַכְּבִים הָאַחֲרוֹנִים.
rashi.eng: *and the rear guard.* the tribe of Dan that traveled last, and they would gather up all those who lingered behind.

notes.194: (tn, Heb): “On the seventh day they rose early, when the dawn ascended.”
notes.195: (tn, Heb): “and they went around the city according to this manner seven times, only on that day they went around the city seven times.”

rashi.heb:
*בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי.* 
שַׁבָּת הָיָה.
rashi.eng: *on the seventh day.* It was the Sabbath.

notes.198: (tn, Heb): “for the Lord has given to you the city.” The verbal form is a perfect, probably indicating certitude here.

notes.199: (tn): Or “dedicated to the Lord.” To make the city set apart for the Lord would involve annihilating all the people and animals and placing its riches in the Lord’s treasury (vv. 19, 21, 24).

rashi.heb:
*וְהָיְתָה הָעִיר חֵרֶם.* 
הֶקְדֵּשׁ, כִּי הַיּוֹם שַׁבַּת קֹדֶשׁ, וְרָאוּי לִהְיוֹת קֹדֶשׁ שָׁלָל הַנִּשְׁלָל בּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *And the city shall be devoted.* consecrated [belonging to “Hekdesh”]. For the day was the Holy Sabbath; hence it was appropriate that the booty which was taken thereon be consecrated.

notes.201: (tn, Heb): “Only you keep [away] from what is set apart [to the Lord] so that you might not, as you are setting [it] apart, take some of what is set apart [to the Lord] and make the camp of Israel set apart [to destruction by the Lord] and bring trouble on it.”

rashi.heb:
*וַעֲכַרְתֶּם.* 
לְשׁוֹן מַיִם עֲכוּרִים.
rashi.eng: *and trouble.* Heb. וַעֲכַרְתֶּם, an expression of turbid water (מַיִם עֲכוּרִים).

notes.202: (tn, Heb): “it is holy to the Lord.”

notes.203: (tc, Heb): “and the people shouted and they blew the rams’ horns.” The initial statement (“and the people shouted”) seems premature, since the verse goes on to explain that the battle cry followed the blowing of the horns. The statement has probably been accidentally duplicated from what follows. It is omitted in the LXX.
notes.206: (tn, Heb): “they shouted with a loud shout.”
notes.208: (tn, Heb): “and the people went up into the city, each one straight ahead, and they captured the city.”

notes.209: (tn, Heb): “all which was in the city.”

notes.210: (tn, Heb): “the house of the woman, the prostitute.”
notes.211: (tn, Heb): “and bring out from there the woman and all who belong to her as you swore on oath to her.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּבֹאוּ הַנְּעָרִים הַמְרַגְּלִים.* 
כָּאן הָיוּ צְרִיכִים זֵירוּז וְנַעֲשׂוּ כִּנְעָרִים זְרִיזִים, וּבַלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן הָיוּ כְּמַלְאָכִים שֶׁשָּׁמְרוּ עַצְמָן מִן הָעֲבֵירָה עִם רָחָב הַזּוֹנָה, לְכָךְ נִקְרְאוּ שָׁם מַלְאָכִים, וּלְכָךְ נִקְרְאוּ: אֲנָשִׁים, מַלְאָכִים, נְעָרִים.
rashi.eng: *And the young men who were spies went in.* here they needed speed, and therefore acted as lively young men. On the first night they were like angels, for they kept themselves from sinning with Rahab the harlot. Therefore, there they were called מַלְאָכִים [lit., angels]. And therefore, they were called men, angels, and young men.

notes.214: (tn, Heb): “the treasury of the house of the Lord.” Technically the Lord did not have a “house” yet, so perhaps this refers to the tabernacle using later terminology.

notes.216: (tn, Heb): the house of her father.”
notes.217: (tn, Heb): Or “among the Israelites”; “in the midst of Israel.”
notes.218: (map): For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

notes.219: (tn): Normally the Hiphil of שָׁבַע (shava’) has a causative sense (“make [someone] take an oath”; see Josh 2:17, 20), but here (see also Josh 23:7) no object is stated or implied. If Joshua is calling divine judgment down upon the one who attempts to rebuild Jericho, then “make a solemn appeal [to God as judge]” or “pronounce a curse” would be an appropriate translation. However, the tone seems stronger. Joshua appears to be announcing the certain punishment of the violator. 1 Kgs 16:34, which records the fulfillment of Joshua’s prediction, supports this. Casting Joshua in a prophetic role, it refers to Joshua’s statement as the “word of the Lord” spoken through Joshua.
notes.221: (tc): The LXX omits “Jericho.” It is probably a scribal addition.
notes.222: (tn): The Hebrew phrase אָרוּר לִפְנֵי יְהוָה (’arur lifney y�hvah, “cursed [i.e., condemned] before the Lord”) also occurs in 1 Sam 26:19.
notes.223: (tn, Heb): “With his firstborn he will lay its foundations and with his youngest he will erect its gates.” The Hebrew verb יַצִּיב (yatsiv, “he will erect”) is imperfect, not jussive, suggesting Joshua’s statement is a prediction, not an imprecation.

rashi.heb:
*בִּבְכֹרוֹ יְיַסְּדֶנָּה וּבִצְעִירוֹ.* 
בִּתְחִלַּת יְסוֹד שֶׁיִּבְנֶה בָּהּ יָמוּת בְּנוֹ הַבְּכוֹר, וְיִקְבְּרֶנוּ וְיֵלֵךְ עַד שֶׁיָּמוּת הַצָּעִיר בִּגְמַר הַמְּלָאכָה, הִיא הַצָּבַת הַדְּלָתוֹת.
rashi.eng: *with [the loss of] his first born shall he lay its foundation, and with [the loss of] his youngest son.* At the beginning of the foundation which he builds therein, his first born son will die and he will bury him, and continue [to bury all his sons] until the youngest one dies at the finish of the work, viz. the setting up of the gates.

notes.224: (tn, Heb): “and the report about him was in all the land.” The Hebrew term אֶרֶץ (’erets, “land”) may also be translated “earth.”

notes.225: (tn, Heb): “But the sons of Israel were unfaithful with unfaithfulness concerning what was set apart [to the Lord].”
notes.226: (tn): 1 Chr 2:6 lists a “Zimri” (but no Zabdi) as one of the five sons of Zerah (cf. also 1 Chr 7:17, 18).
notes.227: (tn, Heb): “took from what was set apart [to the Lord].”
notes.228: (tn, Heb): “the anger of the Lord burned against the sons of Israel.” This incident illustrates well the principle of corporate solidarity and corporate guilt. The sin of one man brought the Lord’s anger down upon the entire nation.

notes.229: (map): For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.
notes.230: (map): For the location of Bethel see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.

rashi.heb:
*עִם בֵּית אָוֶן.* 
אֵצֶל בֵּית אָוֶן.
rashi.eng: *beside Beth aven.* [lit., with Beth aven.]

rashi.heb:
*מִקֶּדֶם לְבֵית אֵל.* 
מִמִּזְרַח לְבֵית אֵל.
rashi.eng: *on the east side of Beth-el.* מִקֶּדֶם.

notes.231: (tn, Heb): “and they returned to Joshua and said to him.”
notes.232: (tn, Heb): “Don’t let all the people go up.”
notes.233: (tn, Heb): “Let about two thousand men or about three thousand men go up to defeat Ai.”
notes.234: (tn, Heb): “all the people for they are small.”

notes.235: (tn): The meaning and correct translation of the Hebrew word שְׁבָרִים (sh�varim) is uncertain. The translation “fissures” is based on usage of the plural form of the noun in Ps 60:4 HT (60:2 ET), where it appears to refer to cracks in the earth caused by an earthquake. Perhaps deep ravines or gorges are in view, or the word is a proper noun (“all the way to Shebarim”).
notes.236: (sn): The precise geographical location of the Israelite defeat at this “steep slope” is uncertain.
notes.238: (tn, Heb): “and the heart of the people melted and became water.”

rashi.heb:
*עַד הַשְּׁבָרִים.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) עַד דְּתַבְרוּנוֹן.*
rashi.eng: *to Shebarim.* until they broke them.

notes.239: (sn): Tearing one’s clothes was an outward expression of extreme sorrow (see Gen 37:34; 44:13).
notes.241: (tn, Heb): “and fell on his face to the ground before the ark of the Lord until evening, he and the elders of Israel.”
notes.242: (sn): Throwing dirt on one’s head was an outward expression of extreme sorrow (see Lam 2:10; Ezek 27:30).

rashi.heb:
*וְלוּ הוֹאַלְנוּ.* 
הַלְוַאי נִמְלַכְנוּ לָשֶׁבֶת בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן מִזְרָחָה, בְּאֶרֶץ סִיחוֹן וְעוֹג שֶׁנִכְבְּשָׁה כְּבָר.
rashi.eng: *Would that we had been content.* Would that we had decided to dwell on the east side of the Jordan in the land of Sihon and Og, which has already been conquered.

notes.246: (tn, Heb): “What will you do for your great name?”

rashi.heb:
*וּמַה תַּעֲשֶׂה לְשִׁמְךָ.* 
הַמְשׁוּתָּף בִּשְׁמֵנוּ, זֶהוּ מִדְרָשׁוֹ. וּפְשׁוּטוֹ וּמַה תַּעֲשֶׂה לְשֵׁם גְּבוּרָתְךָ שֶׁיָּצָא כְּבָר, וְעַתָּה יֹאמְרוּ תָּשַׁשׁ כֹּחוֹ.
rashi.eng: *and what will You do for Your great Name?.* which is inherent in our name [i.e., Israel, the שַׂר, or prince, of God.] This is the derash. The peshat is: What will You do for the Name of Your might which has already become famous? For now they will say, His strength has become weakened.

notes.248: (tn, Heb): “Why are you falling on your face?”

rashi.heb:
*קֻם לָךְ.* 
קָם לָךְ כְּתִיב, עָמַד לְךָ מַה שֶּׁהִתְפַּלַּלְתָּ לְפָנַי וְהִזְכַּרְתָּ. דָּבָר אַחֵר: עָמַדְתָּ לְךָ בַּמַּחֲנֶה וְלֹא יָצָאתָ עִמָּהֶם, וַאֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי: (במדבר כז יז), אֲשֶׁר יוֹצִיאֵם וַאֲשֶׁר יְבִיאֵם, (דברים לא כג): כִּי אַתָּה תָּבִיא אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל... וְאָנֹכִי אֶהְיֶה עִמְּךָ: (שם ג כח), כִּי הוּא יַעֲבֹר לִפְנֵי הָעָם הַזֶּה וְהוּא יַנְחִיל אוֹתָם אִם תֵּלֵךְ אַתָּה לִפְנֵיהֶם יַצְלִיחוּ, וְאִם לָאו לֹא יַצְלִיחוּ. דָּבָר אַחֵר: קֻם לָךְ בִּשְׁבִילְךָ זֹאת לָהֶם, לֹא אָמַרְתִּי לְךָ לְהַקְדִּישׁ שְׁלַל הָעִיר.
rashi.eng: *Get up.* The kethib is קֻם לָ [It has arisen, or stayed, for you.] That which you have prayed before Me and mentioned, has stood you in good stead. Another explanation is: You stayed in camp, and did not go out with them, while I said: “And who will lead them out [to battle] and who will bring them [back].” “For you shall bring the children of Israel and I shall be with you.” “For he will cross before this nation and he will cause them to inherit.” If you go before them, they will succeed, and if not, they will not succeed. Another explanation is: קוּם לָ, [explaining לָ as: On your account] On your account this has befallen them. I did not tell you to consecrate the booty of the city.

notes.249: (tn, Heb): “They have violated my covenant which I commanded them.”
notes.250: (tn, Heb): “what was set apart [to the Lord].”
notes.251: (tn, Heb): “and also they have stolen, and also they have lied, and also they have placed [them] among their items.”

notes.252: (tn, Heb): “they turn [the] back before their enemies because they are set apart [to destruction by the Lord].”
notes.253: (tn): The second person pronoun is plural in Hebrew, indicating these words are addressed to the entire nation.
notes.254: (tn, Heb): “what is set apart [to destruction by the Lord] from your midst.”

notes.255: (tn, Heb): “what is set apart [to destruction by the Lord] [is] in your midst.”
notes.256: (tn, Heb): “remove what is set apart [i.e., to destruction by the Lord] from your midst.”

rashi.heb:
*לַבָּתִּים.* 
יֵשׁ בְּמִשְׁפָּחָה אַחַת הַרְבֵּה בָּתֵּי אָבוֹת.
rashi.eng: *by households.* One family contained many households.

rashi.heb:
*לַגְּבָרִים.* 
לְרָאשֵׁי גּוּלְגּוֹלֶת, כָּל אַנְשֵׁי הַבַּיִת יָבֹאוּ לַגּוֹרָל.
rashi.eng: *man by man.* by heads; all the men of the household were to come to the casting of lots.

notes.261: (tn, Heb): “with what was set apart [to the Lord].”

rashi.heb:
*(תוספת) יִשָּׂרֵף בָּאֵשׁ.* 
הָאֹהֶל וְהַמִּטַּלְטְלִין.
rashi.eng: *[Supplement] shall be burned with fire.* The tent and the movable property.

rashi.heb:
*אֹתוֹ וְאֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ.* 
כַּדִּין הַמְפוֹרָשׁ לְּמַטָּה (להלן פסוק כה): אוֹתוֹ וְהַבְּהֵמָה בִּסְקִילָה, וְהַזָּקֵף שֶׁהוּא עַל 'בָּאֵשׁ' מוֹכִיחַ שֶׁהוּא נִפְרָד 'מֵאוֹתוֹ', שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ מִקְרָאוֹת שֶׁהַטַּעַם מְחַלְּקָן, כְּמוֹ (דברים יא ל): אַחֲרֵי דֶּרֶךְ מְבוֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ, שֶׁ'אַחֲרֵי' מוּפְלָג 'מִדֶּרֶךְ' עַל יְדֵי הַטַּעַם, וְכֵן פִּתְרוֹנוֹ: הַנִּלְכָּד בַּחֵרֶם יִשָּׂרֵף בָּאֵשׁ, הָרָאוּי לִישָּׂרֵף כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּפֹרָשׁ לְּמַטָּה.
rashi.eng: *he and all that he has.* according to the law specified below: He and the cattle by lapidation. The accent zakef which appears over the word: בָּאֵשׁ [with fire] indicates that it is separate from אֹתוֹ [he]; for we find verses which the accent divides, such as: הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ אַחֲרֵי דֶרֶ מְבוֹא, “far past [the Jordan], the way of the going down of the sun,” in which אַחֲרֵי [far past] is separated from דֶרֶ [the way] by the accent. And this is its interpretation: And he that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burned with fire that which is fit to be burned, as is explained below.

rashi.heb:
*אֹתוֹ וְאֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ.* 
כַּדִּין הָאָמוּר לְּמַטָּה, וְזֶה מִקְרָא קָצָר, וְדוֹמֶה לוֹ (שמואל ב ה ח): כָּל מַכֵּה יְבֻסִי וְיִגַּע בַּצִּנּוֹר, לֹא פֵּירַשׁ מַה יִּהְיֶה לוֹ. וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים (א יא ו) פֵּירַשׁ: יִהְיֶה לְרֹאשׁ, אַף כָּאן לֹא פֵּירַשׁ מַה יִּהְיֶה בְּ'אוֹתוֹ וְכָל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ' וּלְמַטָּה פֵּירַשׁ.
rashi.eng: *He and all that he has.* according to the law explained below. This is a brief verse, and similar to it: “whosoever smites the Jebusites and gets up to the tower.” He does not explain what will be done to him. In (I) Chronicles, however, he explains: ‘shall be chief.’ Here also, he did not specify what would be done to ‘him and all that he has,’ and below he specifies.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּקְרֵב אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.* 
לִפְנֵי הַחֹשֶׁן, מָקוֹם שֶׁהַשְּׁבָטִים כְּתוּבִים, וּמָסַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא סִימָן, שֶׁהַשֵּׁבֶט שֶׁחָטָא אַבְנוֹ כָּהָה, וְכָהֲתָה אַבְנוֹ שֶׁל יְהוּדָה.
rashi.eng: *and brought Israel near.* before the ‘hoshen,’ the place where the [names of] the tribes were inscribed. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave him a sign that the tribe which sinned, his stone would fade; and Judah’s stone faded.

notes.264: (tn): See the note on “Zabdi” in 1 Chr 7:1.
notes.265: (tn, Heb): “and he selected Zabdi.” The Lord is the apparent subject. The LXX supports reading a passive (Niphal) form here, as does the immediate context.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּקְרֵב אֶת מִשְׁפַּחַת יְהוּדָה.* 
לְגוֹרָל אֶחָד קֵרַב רָאשֵׁי הַמִּשְׁפָּחוֹת, אָדָם אֶחָד מִכָּל הַמִּשְׁפָּחָה וְהִטִּילוּ גּוֹרָל עַל מִי יִפּוֹל, וְאַחַר כָּךְ עַל כָּל בָּתֵּי אָבוֹת שֶׁל אוֹתָהּ מִשְׁפָּחָה, וּבָא אָדָם אֶחָד מִכָּל בֵּית אָב לְגוֹרָל, וְאַחַר כֵּן בָּאוּ כָּל אַנְשֵׁי אוֹתוֹ הַבַּיִת.
rashi.eng: *and he brought near the family of Judah.* to a casting of lots. He brought near the heads of the families, one man from each family, and they cast lots on whom it would fall, and afterwards on each household, i.e., one man of each household came to the lot casting, and afterwards all the men of that household came.

notes.266: (tn, Heb): “his”; the referent (Zabdi) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*שִׂים־נָא כָבוֹד.* 
הִתְחִיל לְהוֹצִיא לַעַז עַל הַגּוֹרָל, אָמַר לוֹ: בְּגוֹרָל אַתָּה בָּא עָלַי, אַתָּה וְאֶלְעָזָר הַכֹּהֵן גְּדוֹלֵי הַדּוֹר אַתֶּם; הַטֵּל הַגּוֹרָל עַל שְׁנֵיכֶם, וְיִפּוֹל עַל הָאֶחָד. אָמַר לוֹ: שִׂים־נָא כָבוֹד, בְּבַקָּשָׁה מִמְּךָ, אַל תּוֹצִיא לַעַז עַל הַגּוֹרָלוֹת שֶׁבּוֹ עֲתִידָה הָאָרֶץ לֵיחָלֵק.
rashi.eng: *give, I pray you, glory.* He began to criticize the method of casting lots [by which his guilt had been established]. He said: By casting lots are you coming upon me [to establish my guilt]? If a lot were cast between you and Eleazar the two greats of the generation, it would fall on one [of you]. Said he to him: “I ask you not to find fault with the method of casting lots, through which method the land is destined to be divided.”

notes.269: (tn, Heb): “like this and like this I did.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּעַן עָכָן.* 
רָאָה בְּנֵי יְהוּדָה נֶאֱסָפִים לְמִלְחָמָה, אָמַר: מוּטָב שֶׁאָמוּת אֲנִי לְבַדִּי וְאַל יֵהָרְגוּ כַּמָּה אֲלָפִים מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
rashi.eng: *And Achan answered.* He saw the children of Judah [his tribe] assembling for war [in loyalty for one of their own]; and said [to himself]: It is better that I alone die rather than many thousands of Israel be killed.

rashi.heb:
*וְכָזֹאת וְכָזֹאת עָשִׂיתִי.* 
גַּם בַּחֲרָמִים אֲחֵרִים בִּימֵי משֶׁה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (במדבר כא ב): וְהַחֲרַמְתִּי אֶת עָרֵיהֶם.
rashi.eng: *and thus and thus have I done.* also with other devoted things during Moses’ time, as it is stated: “and I will devote their cities.”

notes.270: (tn, Heb): “Shinar,” a reference to Babylon (cf. Gen 10:10; 11:2; 14:1). Many modern translations retain the Hebrew name “Shinar” (cf. NEB, NRSV) but some use the more familiar “Babylon” (cf. NIV, NLT).

rashi.heb:
*וָאֵרֶא בַשָּׁלָל.* 
הִתְבּוֹנַנְתִּי בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה (דברים כ יד): וְאָכַלְתָּ [אֶת־שְׁלַל] וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *When I saw among the spoils.* I reflected upon that which is written in the Torah: “And you shall eat up the spoils of your enemies.”

rashi.heb:
*אַדֶּרֶת שִׁנְעָר.* 
תַּרְגּוּמוֹ: אִיצְטְלָא (דְּמֵילָתָא) בַּבְלִי, שֶׁכָּל מֶלֶךְ שֶׁלֹּא קָנָה לוֹ פַּלְטֵרִין בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, לֹא נִתְקָרְרָה דַּעְתּוֹ בְּמַלְכוּתוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ירמיהו ג יט): וְאֶתֵּן־לָךְ אֶרֶץ חֶמְדָּה נַחֲלַת צְבִי צִבְאוֹת גּוֹיִם, וְהָיָה לְמֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל פַּלְטֵרִין בִּירִיחוֹ, וּכְשֶׁהָיָה בָּא לְכָאן לוֹבֵשׁ אוֹתָם.
rashi.eng: *a Babylonish garment.* As the Targum renders: a Babylonish garment, for any sovereign who had not acquired a palace in the Land of Israel, experienced no satisfaction from his reign, as it is stated: “And I give you a coveted land, an inheritance desired by hosts of nations.” And the king of Babylonia had a palace in Jericho, and when he would come here he would wear them (sic).

notes.272: (tn, Heb): “Look, [it was] hidden in his tent, and the silver was beneath it.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּרֻצוּ הָאֹהֱלָה.* 
שֶׁלֹּא יַקְדִּימוּ שֵׁבֶט יְהוּדָה וְיִטְּלוּהָ מִשָּׁם לְהַכְחִישׁ אֶת הַגּוֹרָל.
rashi.eng: *and they ran to the tent.* lest the tribe of Judah arrive first and take it from there to cast a doubt on the efficacy of the lots.

notes.273: (tn, Heb): “poured out,” probably referring to the way the silver pieces poured out of their container.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּצִּקֻם.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) וְאַתִּיכוּנוּן, וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ (סנהדרין מד א): בָּא וַחֲבָטָן לִפְנֵי הַמָּקוֹם, אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, עַל אֵלּוּ יִפְּלוּ רוּבָּן שֶׁל סַנְהֶדְרִין.
rashi.eng: *and laid them out.* And they melted them. And our Rabbis state: He threw them down before the Omnipresent. He said before Him, “Lord of the Universe, For these [insignificant articles] shall the majority of the Sanhedrin fall?”

notes.274: (tn): Or “Trouble” The name is “Achor” in Hebrew, which means “disaster” or “trouble” (also in v. 26).

rashi.heb:
*וְאֶת בָּנָיו וְגוֹ' וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל.* 
לִרְאוֹת בְּרִדּוּיוֹ וְיִוַּסְּרוּ מִלַּעֲשׂוֹת כָּמוֹהוּ.
rashi.eng: *and his sons, and his daughters.* to witness his chastisement, and so that they be deterred from doing as He [had done].

rashi.heb:
*וְאֶת שׁוֹרוֹ וְאֶת חֲמֹרוֹ.* 
לְאַבְּדָם, כְּמָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (לעיל פסוק טו): וְהָיָה הַנִּלְכָּד בַּחֵרֶם יִשָּׂרֵף בָּאֵשׁ אֹתוֹ וְכָל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ.
rashi.eng: *and his ox and his ass.* to destroy them, as it was said: And it shall be, he that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burned with fire, he and all that he has.

notes.275: (tn): Or “trouble.” The word is “achor” in Hebrew (also in the following clause).
notes.276: (tc, Heb): “and they burned them with fire and they stoned them with stones.” These words are somewhat parenthetical in nature and are omitted in the LXX; they may represent a later scribal addition.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּרְגְּמוּ אֹתוֹ... אֶבֶן.* 
שֶׁחִלֵּל אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
rashi.eng: *and they stoned him etc..* for he had violated the Sabbath.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּשְׂרְפוּ אֹתָם.* 
הָאֹהֶל וְהַמִּטַּלְטְלִין.
rashi.eng: *and burned them.* the tent and the movable property.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּסְקְלוּ אֹתָם.* 
הַשּׁוֹר וְהַבְּהֵמָה.
rashi.eng: *and stoned them.* the ox and the [other] animals.

notes.277: (tc, Heb): “to this day.” The phrase “to this day” is omitted in the LXX and may represent a later scribal addition.

notes.279: (tn, Heb): “Take with you all the people of war and arise, go up against Ai!”
notes.280: (tn, Heb): “I have given into our hand.” The verbal form, a perfect, is probably best understood as a perfect of certitude, indicating the certainty of the action.

notes.281: (map): For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

rashi.heb:
*תָּבֹזּוּ לָכֶם.* 
וְאַל תַּחֲרִימוּ הַשָּׁלָל עוֹד.
rashi.eng: *only you shall take as spoils to yourselves.* do not cause the spoils to be “cherem” [doomed] anymore [as you did in Jericho].

notes.282: (tn): “And Joshua and all the people of war arose to go up [against] Ai.”

rashi.heb:
*הַתִּיקֵנוּ אוֹתָם.* 
לְשׁוֹן תִּיק, שֶׁנּוֹצִיאֵם מִתִּיק הָעִיר, דישפורי"ר בְּלַעַז (לְהוֹצִיא, לִשְׁלוֹף). וְיֵשׁ לְפוֹתְרוֹ לְשׁוֹן נְתִיקָה, כְּמוֹ (ירמיהו יב ג): הַתִּיקֵם כְּצֹאן לְטִבְחָה.
rashi.eng: *we have drawn them out.* Heb. הַתִּיֵקְנוּ, an expression of תִּיק, a sheath, i.e., until we have taken them out of the sheath [the protection afforded them by the fortifications of] the city. Defourrer in Fr. [to unsheathe, from fourreau, a sheath]. We may also interpret it as an expression of נְתִיקָה, drawing out, as: Draw them out like flocks to the slaughter.

rashi.heb:
*וְהוֹרַשְׁתֶּם.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) וּתְתָרְכוּן.

notes.291: (map): For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
notes.292: (tn, Heb): “and they stayed between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai.”
notes.293: (tn, Heb): “in the midst of the people.”

rashi.heb:
*מִיָּם לָעַי.* 
שֶׁהָעַי מִקֶּדֶם לְבֵית אֵל, וּבֵית אֵל מִיָּם לָעַי.
rashi.eng: *on the west side of Ai.* for Ai was on the east side of Beth-el and Beth-el was on the west side of Ai.

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּלֶן יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּתוֹךְ הָעָם.* 
לִהְיוֹת נָכוֹן בְּהַשְׁכָּמַת הַבֹּקֶר.
rashi.eng: *and Joshua lodged among the people.* to be ready early in the morning.
