notes.298: (tn, Heb): “them” (referring to “the people” in the previous clause, which requires a plural pronoun). Since the translation used “army” in the previous clause, a singular pronoun (“it”) is required in English.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּעַל הוּא.* 
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַמָּקוֹם, אִם הוּא עוֹבֵר לִפְנֵיהֶם עוֹבְרִין, וְאִם לָאו אֵין עוֹבְרִין.
rashi.eng: *and he went up.* as the Omnipresent had said to him: “If he crosses before them they will cross and if not, they will not cross.”

notes.299: (tn, Heb): “All the people of war who were with him went up and approached and came opposite the city.”
notes.300: (tn, Heb): “and the valley [was] between them and Ai.”

notes.301: (map): For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּקַּח כַּחֲמֵשֶׁת אֲלָפִים אִישׁ.* 
אוֹרֵב אַחַר אוֹרֵב, אֶחָד קָרוֹב לָעִיר מֵחֲבֵירוֹ.
rashi.eng: *And he took about five thousand men.* one ambush, following the other ambush, closer to the city than its fellow.

notes.302: (tn): Some Hebrew mss read, “spent the night in.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּשִׂימוּ הָעָם.* 
שִׂימָה זוֹ לְשׁוֹן הַזְמָנָה, סָמוּךְ לַחוֹמָה לְהִלָּחֵם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּבֶן הֲדַד (מלכים א כ ל): שִׂימוּ עַל הָעִיר, וַיָּשִׂימוּ.
rashi.eng: *And the people set.* This setting is an expression of preparation near the wall, to wage war, as it is stated concerning the son of Hadad in (I) Kings (20:12): “Set upon the city. And they set.”

rashi.heb:
*וְאֶת עֲקֵבוֹ.* 
וְאֶת אָרְבּוֹ, כְּמוֹ (בראשית כז לו): וַיַּעְקְבֵנִי.
rashi.eng: *and their liers in wait.* Heb. עֲקֵבוֹ their liers in wait, like: “For he has tricked me (וַיַּעַקְבֵנִי)”

rashi.heb:
*וַיֵּלֶךְ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּא בְּתוֹךְ הָעֵמֶק.* 
אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ (סנהדרין מד ב) שֶׁלָּן בְּעוֹמְקָהּ שֶׁל הֲלָכָה.
rashi.eng: *And Joshua went that night into the midst of the valley.* Our Rabbis said that he lodged in the depth of the Law.

notes.303: (tn, Heb): “When the king of Ai saw, the men of Ai hurried and rose early and went out to meet Israel for battle, he and all his people at the meeting place before the Arabah.”
notes.305: (tn, Heb): “that (there was) an ambush for him behind the city.”

rashi.heb:
*לַמּוֹעֵד.* 
לִזְמַן הַיּוֹם, שֶׁנּוֹעֲצוּ יַחַד מֵאֶתְמוֹל בְּאוֹתוֹ שָׁעָה נֵצֵא, שֶׁהָיוּ מְנַחֲשִׁים וּמְעוֹנְנִים.
rashi.eng: *at a time appointed.* At the time of day which they had planned [or been advised] on the preceding day, “at that time we will go out,” for they were soothsayers and diviners.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּנָּגְעוּ.* 
לְשׁוֹן נֶגַע (כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ:) וְאִתְּבַרוּ, הֶרְאוּ עַצְמָן כְּאִלּוּ הֵם נִגָּפִים לִפְנֵיהֶם.
rashi.eng: *pretended to be beaten.* Heb. וַיִּנָּגְעוּ, an expression of a plague [or beating]. [Jonathan renders] and were broken. They showed themselves as though they were beaten before them.

notes.309: (tc): The LXX omits the words “or Bethel.” For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
notes.310: (tn, Heb): “who did not go out after Israel.”

notes.311: (tn, Heb): “it”; the referent (the city of Ai) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*נְטֵה בַּכִּידוֹן.* 
הוּא הָיָה סִימָן לָאוֹרֵב לָצֵאת מִן הַמַּאֲרָב, בִּרְאוֹתוֹ הַכִּידוֹן נָטוּי עַל הָעִיר. כִּידוֹן שפיד"ו בְּלַעַז (רוֹמַח, חַנִית).
rashi.eng: *Stretch out the spear.* This was the signal for the group lying in ambush to emerge from the ambush when they would see the spear stretched out toward the city. espada in Spanish, a sword.

notes.313: (tn, Heb): “and they saw, and look.” The Hebrew term הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”) draws attention to the scene and invites the audience to view the events from the perspective of the men of Ai.
notes.314: (tn, Heb): “and there was not in them hands to flee here or there.” The Hebrew term יָדַיִם (yadayim, “hands”) is idiomatic for “strength.”

rashi.eng: *power.* lit., hands.

rashi.heb:
*וְהָעָם הַנָּס הַמִּדְבָּר.* 
יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנָּסוּ אֶל הַמִּדְבָּר כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לְמַעְלָה, נֶהְפַּךְ לְהִלָּחֵם אֶל הָרוֹדֵף.
rashi.eng: *and the people that fled to the desert.* The Israelites who fled to the desert, as it is stated above, turned back to fight upon the pursuers.

notes.315: (tn, Heb): “and that the smoke of the city ascended.”

notes.316: (tn, Heb): “and these went out from the city to meet them and they were for Israel in the middle, some on this side, and others on the other side.”

rashi.heb:
*וְאֵלֶּה יָצְאוּ מִן הָעִיר.* 
הָאוֹרֵב שֶׁהִצִּית אֶת הָעִיר.
rashi.eng: *And the others came out of the city.* the ambush who had set fire to the city.

notes.318: (tn, Heb): “in the field, in the desert in which they chased them.”
notes.319: (tc, Heb): “and all of them fell by the edge of the sword until they were destroyed.” The LXX omits the words, “and all of them fell by the edge of the sword.” They may represent a later scribal addition.

notes.321: (tn, Heb): “Joshua did not draw back his hand which held out the curved sword until he had annihilated all the residents of Ai.”

notes.322: (tn, Heb): “according to the word of the Lord which he commanded Joshua.”

notes.323: (tn, Heb): “and made it a permanent mound, a desolation, to this day.”

notes.324: (tn, Heb): “on a tree until evening.” The words “leaving him exposed” are supplied in the translation for clarity.
notes.325: (sn): For the legal background of this action, see Deut 21:22-23.

rashi.heb:
*אָז יִבְנֶה וְגוֹ'.* 
פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ כְּתוּבָה מוּקְדָּם וּמְאוּחָר, שֶׁמִּיּוֹם שֶׁעָבְרוּ אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן עָשָׂה כֵּן.
rashi.eng: *Then Joshua, etc..* This section is written in the manner of ‘earlier’ and ‘later’ [events combined], for on the day they crossed the Jordan he did so.

notes.327: (tn, Heb): “as it is written in the scroll of the law of Moses, an altar of whole stones on which no one had wielded iron.” The expression “whole stones” refers to stones in their natural condition, i.e., not carved or shaped artificially with tools (“wielded iron”).

notes.329: (tn, Heb): “and he wrote there on the stones a duplicate of the law of Moses which he wrote before the sons of Israel.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּכְתָּב־שָׁם עַל הָאֲבָנִים.* 
הֵן הֵנָּה הָאֲבָנִים הָאֲמוּרִים לְמַעְלָה, לְאַחַר מַעֲשֶׂה זֶה קִפְּלוּ (קלפו) הַסִּיד מֵעֲלֵיהֶם וֶהֱבִיאוּם הַגִּלְגָּל.
rashi.eng: *And he wrote there on the stones.* They are the aforementioned stones. After this event [of building the altar] they peeled the lime off them and brought them to Gilgal.

notes.332: (tn, Heb): “like the resident alien, like the citizen.” The language is idiomatic, meaning that both groups were treated the same, at least in this instance.
notes.333: (tn, Heb): “as Moses, the Lord’s servant, commanded to bless the people, Israel, formerly.” Moses’ earlier instructions are found in Deut 11:29.

rashi.heb:
*לְבָרֵךְ אֶת הָעָם יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה.* 
לְהַקְדִּים בְּרָכוֹת לִקְלָלוֹת: בָּרוּךְ הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה פֶסֶל וּמַסֵּכָה.
rashi.eng: *to bless the people of Israel first.* to pronounce the blessings before the curses: Blessed be the man who will not make a graven or molten image.

notes.335: (tn, Heb): “There was not a word from all which Moses commanded that Joshua did not read aloud.”

notes.337: (tn, Heb): “When all the kings who were beyond the Jordan heard.”
notes.339: (tn, Heb): “all the coast of the Great Sea.” The “Great Sea” was the typical designation for the Mediterranean Sea.

notes.341: (tn, Heb): “they gathered together to fight against Joshua and Israel [with] one mouth.”

notes.342: (map): For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

notes.343: (tc, Heb): “and they went and [?].” The root and meaning of the verb form יִצְטַיָּרוּ (yitstayyaru) are uncertain. The form is most likely a corruption of יִצְטַיָּדוּ (yitstayyadu), read by some Hebrew mss and ancient versions, from the root צוּד (tsud, “take provisions,” BDB 845 s.v. II צוד) which also occurs in v. 11. Note NRSV “they went and prepared provisions”; cf. NEB “They went and disguised themselves”; NIV “they went as a delegation.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּעֲשׂוּ גַּם הֵמָּה בְּעָרְמָה.* 
כְּמוֹ שֶׁעָשׂוּ בְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב בְּעָרְמָה (בראשית לד) וּבַחֲמוֹר אֲבִי שְׁכֶם שֶׁהָיָה חִוִּי, וְיוֹשְׁבֵי גִּבְעוֹן מִן הַחִוִּי הָיוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמוּר בָּעִנְיָן.
rashi.eng: *And they also acted with wile.* Just as Jacob’s sons dealt cunningly with Hamor the father of Shechem who was a Hivite; and the inhabitants of Gibeon were also from the Hivites, as it is stated in this episode.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּצְטַיָּרוּ.* 
עָשׂוּ עַצְמָם כְּהוֹלְכִים בִּשְׁלִיחוּת, לְשׁוֹן (ירמיהו מט יד): וְצִיר בַּגּוֹיִם שֻׁלַּח, וְכָל תֵּיבָה שֶׁתְּחִלַּת יְסוֹדָהּ צָדִ"י, כְּשֶׁהִיא מִתְפַּעֶלֶת ל' מִתְפַּעֵל, אוֹ נִתְפַּעֵל, בָּאָה טֵי"ת בְּתוֹכָהּ וְחוֹלֶקֶת אֶת אוֹתִיוֹת שָׁרְשֵׁי הַתֵּיבָה, כְּמוֹ (בראשית מד טז): מַה נִּצְטַדָּק, מִגִּזְרַת צֶדֶק, שֶׁאוֹמֵר נִּצְטַדַּק, וְכֵן (דניאל ד ל): גִּשְׁמֵהּ יִצְטַבַּע, מִגִּזְרַת צֶבַע.
rashi.eng:
*disguised as ambassadors.* 
They made themselves like message carriers, from the expression of: “(וְצִיר) And a messenger was sent among the nations.” Now, every word, the beginning of whose root is ‘zade,’ when it is used as reflexive in the form of מתפעל or נתפעל, a ‘teth’ comes in the middle thereof, and separates the root letters of the word, like: מַה נִּצְטַדָּק ‘How will we justify ourselves?’ from the root צדק, [that he says נִצְטַדָּק,] and so: גשמה יִצְטַבַּע ‘his body will be bathed,’ from צבע.

rashi.heb:
*שַׂקִּים בָּלִים.* 
שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִרְאִים כְּבָאִים מֵאֶרֶץ רְחוֹקָה.
rashi.eng: *wine bottles, rotten.* so that they should appear like people coming from a distant land.

rashi.heb:
*וּמְצֹרָרִים.* 
לְשׁוֹן מְבוּקָּעִים, לְשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי: צִירְיָא דְּחִיטֵּי דְּמָצְרִי זִיקֵי.
rashi.eng: *and tied up.* a synonym for מְבַקְּעִים, split., This is an Aramaic expression, as דחיטי ציריה, ‘the splits of the wheat kernels,’ דמיצרי זיקי, ‘which split the sacks.’

notes.344: (tn, Heb): “all the bread of their provisions.”

rashi.heb:
*נִקֻּדִים.* 
ארשי"ץ בְּלַעַז (שְׂרוּפִים כֶּעֵין צְנִימִים), לְשׁוֹן מוֹקֵד, וְכֵן תִּרְגְּמוֹ יוֹנָתָן: כִּסְנִין.
rashi.eng: *and all the bread… was dry and mouldy.* arsin in French, an expression of מוּקָד, burned [or toasted], and so did Jonathan render כִסְנִין.

rashi.heb:
*אוּלַי בְּקִרְבִּי אַתָּה יוֹשֵׁב.* 
שֶׁמָּא מִיּוֹשְׁבֵי הָאָרֶץ אַתֶּם.
rashi.eng: *Perhaps you dwell in my midst.* Perhaps you are from the inhabitants of the land?

notes.350: (tn, Heb): “the report about him, all that he did in Egypt.”

notes.352: (tn, Heb): “in the day we went out to come to you.”

rashi.heb:
*הִצְטַיַּדְנוּ.* 
לְשׁוֹן צֵדָה, כְּשֶׁהוֹצֵאנוּהוּ לְצֵדָה לַדֶּרֶךְ.
rashi.eng: *we took… for our provision.* Heb. הִצְטַיַּדְנוּ, an expression of צֵידָה provisions, i.e., when we took it out for provisions for the journey.

notes.354: (tn, Heb): “took.” This probably means they tasted some of the food to make sure it was stale.
notes.355: (tn, Heb): “but they did not ask the mouth of the Lord.” This refers to seeking the Lord’s will and guidance through an oracle.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּקְחוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים מִצֵּידָם.* 
קִבְּלוּ דִּבְרֵיהֶם, שֶׁצָּדוּם בְּפִיהֶם, לְשׁוֹן (שמות כא יג): וַאֲשֶׁר לֹא צָדָה.
rashi.eng: *And the men took of their provision.* They accepted their words for they captured them with their mouths [מִצֵּידָם meaning from their hunting or capturing] an expression of: “and he who did not (צֵידָה) hunt.”

notes.357: (tn, Heb): “Joshua made peace with them and made a treaty with them to let them live, and the leaders of the community swore an oath to them.”

notes.358: (tn, Heb): “At the end of three days, after they made the treaty with them, they heard that they were neighbors to them and in their midst they were living.”

notes.359: (tn, Heb): “by the Lord God of Israel.”

notes.363: (tn, Heb): “This is what we will do to them, keeping them alive so there will not be upon us anger concerning the oath which we swore to them.”

notes.364: (tc, Heb): “and the leaders said to them.” The LXX omits the words “and the leaders said to them.”
notes.365: (tn): The vav (ו) consecutive construction in the Hebrew text suggests that the narrative resumes at this point. The LXX reads here, “and they will be,” understanding what follows to be a continuation of the leaders’ words rather than a comment by the narrator.
notes.366: (tn, Heb): “as the leaders said to them.”

notes.367: (sn): Verses 22-27 appear to elaborate on v. 21b.

notes.371: (tn, Heb): “Now you are cursed and a servant will not be cut off from you, woodcutters and water carriers for the house of my God.”

notes.374: (tn, Heb): “so now, look, we are in your hand.”
notes.375: (tn, Heb): “according to what is good and according to what is upright in your eyes to do us, do.”

notes.376: (tn, Heb): “And he did to them so and he rescued them from the hand of the sons of Israel and they did not kill them.”

notes.377: (tn, Heb): “and Joshua made them in that day woodcutters and water carriers for the community, and for the altar of the Lord to this day at the place which he chooses.”

notes.378: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.379: (map): For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.
notes.380: (tn, Heb): “as he had done to Jericho and to its king, so he did to Ai and to its king.”

notes.382: (tn): This statement is subordinated to v. 1 in the Hebrew text, which reads literally, “When Adoni-Zedek…they feared greatly.” The subject of the plural verb at the beginning of v. 2 is probably the residents of Jerusalem.

notes.383: (tn, Heb): “Come up to me and help me.”

notes.384: (tn, Heb): “and they camped against Gibeon and fought against it.”

notes.385: (tn, Heb): “do not let your hand drop from us.”

notes.388: (tn, Heb): “And Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the people of war with him, and all the brave warriors.”

notes.389: (tn, Heb): “I have given them into your hand.” The verbal form is a perfect of certitude, emphasizing the certainty of the action.
notes.390: (tn, Heb): “and not a man [or “one”] of them will stand before you.”

notes.391: (tn, Heb): “Joshua came upon them suddenly, all the night he went up from Gilgal.”

notes.393: (tn, Heb): “he.” The referent is probably Israel (mentioned at the end of the previous sentence in the verse; cf. NIV, NRSV), but it is also possible that the Lord should be understood as the referent (cf. NASB “and He slew them with a great slaughter at Gibeon”), or even Joshua (cf. NEB “and Joshua defeated them utterly in Gibeon”).
notes.394: (tn, Heb): “struck them down with a great striking down.”

notes.397: (tn): Or “heaven” (also in v. 13). The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heaven(s)” or “sky” depending on the context.

notes.398: (tn, Heb): “Then Joshua spoke to the Lord in the day the Lord placed the Amorites before the sons of Israel and he said in the eyes of Israel.” It is uncertain whether the phrase “before the sons of Israel” modifies the verb “placed” (as in the present translation, “delivered the Amorites over to the Israelites”) or the verb “spoke” (“Joshua spoke to the Lord before the sons of Israel in the day the Lord delivered over the Amorites”).

rashi.heb:
*אָז יְדַבֵּר.* 
אָמַר שִׁירָה תַּחַת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ, לְפִי שֶׁאָמַר לַשֶּׁמֶשׁ דּוֹם, דּוֹם מִלּוֹמַר שִׁירָה, וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁהוּא דּוֹמֵם, עוֹמֵד וְאֵינוֹ מְהַלֵּךְ, שֶׁבְּכָל עֵת הִילּוּכוֹ הוּא אוֹמֵר שִׁירָה. וּפְשׁוּטוֹ שֶׁל מִקְרָא: דּוֹם לְשׁוֹן הַמְתָּנָה, כְּמוֹ (שמואל א יד ט): אִם כֹּה יֹאמְרוּ אֵלֵינוּ דֹּמּוּ, וְכֵן (תהלים לז ז): דֹּם לַה'.
rashi.eng: *Then Joshua spoke.* He recited a song instead of the sun, since he bade the sun, “Be silent,” i.e., be silent [by refraining] from reciting [your] song. And as long as it is silent, it stands still and does not continue on its orbit, for all the time of its revolution it recites [its] song. The simple explanation of the verse is, however, (דּוֹם) is an expression of waiting, like: “if they say thus to us, ‘wait!’” (דּוֹמוּ), and so, “wait (דּוֹם) for the Lord.”

rashi.heb:
*וְיָרֵחַ בְּעֵמֶק אַיָּלוֹן.* 
אוֹתוֹ פַּעַם הָיָה הַיָּרֵחַ עוֹמֵד כְּנֶגֶד עֵמֶק אַיָּלוֹן, וְהוּא רָחוֹק מִגִּבְעוֹן, שֶׁהֲרֵי גִּבְעוֹן בִּגְבוּל בִּנְיָמִין וְאַיָּלוֹן בִּגְבוּל דָּן.
rashi.eng: *and moon in the valley of Ajalon.* At that time, the moon was standing opposite the valley of Ajalon, which is far from Gibeon, for Gibeon is within the borders of Benjamin [in the south], and Ajalon is within the borders of Dan [in the north].

notes.399: (tn, Heb): “Is it not written down in the Scroll of the Upright One.” Many modern translations render, “the Scroll [or Book] of Jashar,” leaving the Hebrew name “Jashar” (which means “Upright One”) untranslated. The Scroll of the Upright One was apparently an ancient Israelite collection of songs and prayers (see also 2 Sam 1:18).
notes.400: (tn, Heb): “and did not hurry to set [for] about a full day.”

rashi.heb:
*הֲלֹא הִיא כְתוּבָה.* 
דָּבָר זֶה נִכְתַּב בַּתּוֹרָה, שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ יַעֲקֹב לְיוֹסֵף (בראשית מח יט): וְזַרְעוֹ (שֶׁל אֶפְרַיִם) יִהְיֶה מְלֹא הַגוֹיִם, אֵימָתַי, בְּיוֹם שֶׁעָמְדָה חַמָּה לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ, נִתְמַלֵּא כָּל הָעוֹלָם שִׁמְעוֹ שֶׁל יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, וַיַּעֲמֹד הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ בַּחֲצִי הַשָּׁמַיִם וְלֹא אָץ לָבֹא כְּיוֹם תָּמִים.
rashi.eng: *Is it not written [already] in the book of Jashar?.* This matter is written in the Torah [i.e., the Pentateuch] that Jacob said to Joseph, “His seed [of Ephraim] will fill the nations.” When? On the day that the sun stood still for Joshua, the entire world was filled with Joshua’s fame, and the sun stood still in the midst of the heaven, and it did not hasten to go down exactly a whole day."

notes.403: (tn, Heb): “and appoint by it men to guard them.”

rashi.heb:
*גֹּלּוּ.* 
גַּלְגְּלוּ אֲבָנִים אֶל פִּי הַמְּעָרָה.
rashi.eng: *Roll.* Heb. גֹּלּוּ, “roll (גַּלְגְּלוּ) great stones onto the mouth of the cave.”

notes.404: (tn, Heb): “But [as for] you, don’t stand still, chase after your enemies and attack them from the rear.”
notes.406: (tn, Heb): “has given them into your hand.” The verbal form is a perfect of certitude, emphasizing the certainty of the action.

notes.407: (tn, Heb): “When Joshua and the sons of Israel finished defeating them with a very great defeat until they were destroyed (now the survivors escaped to the fortified cities).” In the Hebrew text the initial temporal clause (“when Joshua…finished”) is subordinated to v. 21 (“the whole army returned”).

notes.408: (tn, Heb): “all the people returned to the camp, to Joshua [at] Makkedah [in] peace.”
notes.409: (tc, Heb): “No man.” The lamed (ל) prefixed to אִישׁ (’ish, “man”) is probably dittographic (note the immediately preceding יִשְׂרָאֵל [isra’el] which ends in lamed, ל); cf. the LXX.
notes.410: (tn, Heb): “no man sharpened [or perhaps, “pointed”] his tongue against the sons of Israel.” Cf. NEB “not a man of the Israelites suffered so much as a scratch on his tongue,” which understands “sharpened” as “scratched” (referring to a minor wound). Most modern translations understand the Hebrew expression “sharpened his tongue” figuratively for opposition or threats against the Israelites.

rashi.heb:
*לֹא חָרַץ לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.* 
הֲרֵי זֶה מִקְרָא קָצָר, לֹא חָרַץ הַחוֹרֵץ לְאִישׁ מִבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת לְשׁוֹנוֹ.
rashi.eng: *none whetted his tongue against any of the children of Israel.* This is a short verse, [the subject being absent in the original, meaning] no whetter whetted his tongue to any of the children of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*חָרַץ.* 
לְשׁוֹן דִּבּוּר הַלָּשׁוֹן, וְכֵן (שמות יא ז): לֹא יֶחֱרַץ כֶּלֶב לְשׁוֹנוֹ, וְכֵן (שמואל ב ה כד): אָז תֶּחֱרָץ, דְּדָוִד תִּקְרָא, תִּצְעַק קוֹל תְּשׁוּאוֹת הַמִּלְחָמָה.
rashi.eng: *whetted.* Heb. חָרַץ, an expression meaning speech of the tongue, and so: “no dog whetted (יֶחֱרָץ) its tongue.” And so: “Then shall you shout (תֶּחֱרָץ),” stated concerning David, “You shall call out, you shall shout a battle cry.”

rashi.heb:
*וְהָאֲשֵׁדוֹת.* 
מָקוֹם שֶׁמֵּי הַגְּבָעוֹת שׁוֹפְכִים.
rashi.eng: *and the falls.* the place where the water of the hills pours down.

notes.444: (tn, Heb): “and Joshua struck them down, from Kadesh Barnea even to Gaza, and all the land of Goshen, even to Gibeon.”

rashi.heb:
*מִקָּדֵשׁ בַּרְנֵע וְעַד עַזָּה.* 
מִצַּד דְּרוֹמִית שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא, מִן הַמִּזְרָח לַמַּעֲרָב, וְלֹא הִסְפִּיק לִכְבּוֹשׁ כָּל הַמֶּצֶר וְנִשְׁאַר מֵעַזָּה עַד הַיָּם, הוּא שֶׁאָמַר לְּמַטָּה: זֹאת הָאָרֶץ הַנִּשְׁאֶרֶת הָעַזָּתִי וְהָאַשְׁדּוֹדִי וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza.* This is from the south side of Eretz Israel from east to west. He was, however, unable to conquer the entire boundary, thus there remained from Gaza to the [Mediterranean] Sea. This is what the Scripture states below: “This is the land that yet remained… the Gazathites, and the Ashdodites, etc.”

notes.446: (map): For location see Map1-D2; Map2-D3; Map3-A2; Map4-C1.

notes.448: (tn, Heb): “and to the kings who [are] from the north in.”
notes.449: (tn, Heb): “Chinneroth,” a city and plain located in the territory of Naphtali in Galilee (BDB 490 s.v. כִּנֶּרֶת, כִּנֲרוֹת). Kinnereth was a city in Galilee located near the Sea of Galilee (Deut 3:17). The surrounding region also became known by this name (1 Kgs 15:20; cf. Matt 14:34), and eventually even the lake itself (Josh 12:3; cf. Luke 5:1).

rashi.heb:
*נֶגֶב כִּנְרוֹת.* 
דְּרוֹם גִּינוֹסָר.
rashi.eng: *south of Chinnaroth.* south of Ginosar.

rashi.heb:
*וּבְנָפוֹת דּוֹר.* 
פִּלְכֵי דּוֹר, קונטדו"ש בְּלַעַז (חֶלְקֵי אָרֶץ, מְחוֹזוֹת).
rashi.eng: *and in the region of Dor.* the provinces of Dor, Contree in French.

rashi.heb:
*מִיָּם.* 
מַעֲרָבָה.

notes.450: (tn): The verb “came” is supplied in the translation (see v. 4).

notes.452: (tn, Heb): “They and all their camps with them came out, a people as numerous as the sand which is on the edge of the sea in multitude, and [with] horses and chariots very numerous.”

notes.455: (tn, Heb): “Joshua and all the people of war with him came upon them at the Waters of Merom suddenly and fell upon them.”

notes.457: (tn): The meaning of the Hebrew name “Misrephoth Maim” is perhaps “lime-kilns by the water” (see HALOT 2:641).

rashi.heb:
*מִשְׂרְפוֹת מַיִם.* 
תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: חֲרִיצֵי יַמָּא, שֶׁעוֹשִׂין חֲרִיצִין וּמֵי הַיָּם יוֹצְאִין לְתוֹכָן, וְנִשְׂרָפִין מֵחוֹם הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְנַעֲשִׂים מֶלַח.
rashi.eng: *Misrephoth-maim.* Jonathan renders: Ditches of the sea, for they would make ditches, into which the sea water would flow and burn up [evaporate] from the heat of the sun, and become salt.

notes.458: (tn, Heb): “burned with fire”; the words “with fire” are redundant in English and have not been included in the translation.

notes.462: (tn, Heb): “burned with fire”; the words “with fire” are redundant in English and have not been included in the translation.

notes.463: (tn, Heb): “and he struck them down with the edge of the sword, he annihilated them.”

rashi.heb:
*הָעֹמְדוֹת עַל תִּלָּם.* 
שֶׁלֹּא נֶהֱרְסָה חוֹמָתָם כְּמוֹ יְרִיחוֹ שֶׁנָּפְלָה חוֹמָתָהּ, וְכֵן הָעַי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהּ (לעיל ח כח): וַיְשִׂימֶהָ תֵּל עוֹלָם שְׁמָמָה.
rashi.eng: *that stood in their strength.* Jonathan renders: whose walls were not destroyed, like Jericho, whose walls fell, and so Ai, concerning which it is stated: “And made it a heap forever, a desolation.”

rashi.heb:
*זוּלָתִי אֶת־חָצוֹר לְבַדָּהּ.* 
בַּמָּסוֹרֶת שְׂרָפָה משֶׁה צִוָּה לוֹ וּמָסַר לוֹ כֵּן. (בראשית רבה וישלח):
rashi.eng: *save Hazor only.* because of a tradition he burned it. Moses commanded and transmitted it to him. In Genesis Rabbah, in the portion entitled: And Jacob sent.

notes.466: (tn, Heb): “but all the people they struck down with the edge of the sword until they destroyed them.”

notes.467: (tn, Heb): “As the Lord commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and Joshua acted accordingly; he did not turn aside a thing from all which the Lord commanded Moses.”

notes.470: (tn, Heb): “and struck them down and killed them.”

rashi.heb:
*הָהָר הֶחָלָק.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) טוּרָא שְׁעִיעַ, מַחֲלִיק, הָהָר הֶחָלָק עַד בַּעַל גָּד בַּמֶּצֶר הַמִּזְרָחִי, וְלֹא הִסְפִּיק לִכְבּוֹשׁ בְּחַיָּיו אֶת כָּל הַמֶּצֶר עַד הַצָּפוֹן.
rashi.eng: *the divided smooth mount.* Onkelos renders these words to be translated as "smooth mount." The smooth mount until Baal-gad at the eastern border. And he didn't manage to conquer the entire border until the north during his lifetime.

rashi.heb:
*בַּעַל גָּד.* 
מֵישַׁר גָּד.
rashi.eng: *Baal gad.* the plain of Gad.

rashi.heb:
*יָמִים רַבִּים עָשָׂה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.* 
בִּגְנוּתוֹ סִפֵּר הַכָּתוּב, שֶׁהָיָה מִתְכַּוֵּון לִדְחוֹת אֶת כִּבּוּשׁ הָאָרֶץ כְּדֵי לְהַאֲרִיךְ יָמָיו, לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (לעיל א י): וְאַתָּה תַּנְחִלֶנָּה אוֹתָם, בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא.
rashi.eng: *Joshua made war a long time with all these kings.* This sentence is a rebuke to Joshua for he intended to delay the conquest of the Land in order to lengthen his lifespan, for it was stated: “And you shall cause them to inherit it.”

notes.473: (tn): The LXX omits this parenthetical note, which may represent a later scribal addition.

notes.475: (tn, Heb): “for from the Lord it was to harden their heart[s] to meet for the battle with Israel, in order to annihilate them, so that they would receive no mercy, in order annihilate them, as the Lord commanded Moses.”

notes.476: (tn, Heb): “went and cut off the Anakites from the hill country.”
notes.477: (tn, Heb): “and from all the hill country of Israel.”

notes.479: (tn, Heb): “according to all which the Lord said to Moses.” The translation assumes this refers to the promise of the land (see 1:3). Another possibility is that it refers to the Lord’s instructions, in which case the phrase could be translated, “just as the Lord had instructed Moses” (so NLT; cf. also NIV “had directed Moses”).

notes.482: (tn, Heb): “beyond the Jordan, toward the rising of the sun.”

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר הִכּוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.* 
בִּימֵי משֶׁה.
rashi.eng: *whom the children of Israel smote.* During the days of Moses.

notes.484: (tc): The MT reads here, “and the middle of the valley,” but the reading “the city in the middle of valley” can be reconstructed on the basis of Josh 13:9, 16.

rashi.heb:
*וְעַד יַבֹּק הַנַּחַל.* 
שֶׁשָּׁם גְּבוּל אֶרֶץ בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן, סוֹף מֶצֶר אֶרֶץ בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן, וּמִשָּׁם וָהָלְאָה הָיוּ בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן מוֹשְׁלִים.
rashi.eng: *and to the river Jabbok.* For there was the border of the land of the children of 'Ammon, the edge of the territory of the land of the children of 'Ammon, and from there on, the children of 'Ammon were ruling.

notes.485: (tn): The words “his kingdom included” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
notes.486: (sn): The Sea of Kinnereth is another name for the Sea of Galilee. See the note on the word “Kinnereth” in 11:2.
notes.487: (sn): The Salt Sea is another name for the Dead Sea.

notes.488: (tn, Heb): “from the remnant of the Rephaites.” The Rephaites were apparently an extremely tall ethnic group. See Deut 2:10-11, 20; 3:11.

rashi.heb:
*וַחֲצִי הַגִּלְעָד גְּבוּל סִיחוֹן.* 
שָׁם הָיָה מֶצֶר מֶמְשֶׁלֶת סִיחוֹן, כְּשֶׁאָמַרְנוּ לְמַעְלָה, שֶׁחֲצִי הַגִּלְעָד הָיָה שֶׁלּוֹ, וְזֶה חֲצִי הַשֵּׁנִי שֶׁל עוֹג.
rashi.eng: *and half Gilead, the border of Sihon.* There was the border of Sihon’s realm, as it was stated above (2) that half of Gilead was his, and this second half was 'Og’s.

notes.491: (tn, Heb): “Joshua gave it to the tribes of Israel as a possession according to their allotted portions.”

notes.493: (tn): The words “the land of” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
