rashi.heb:
*מִבְצַר צֹר.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) קִרְוִין כְּרִיכָן קִרְוֵי תּוּקְפָא.
rashi.eng: *to the fortress city of the rock.* fortified cities, strong cities.

rashi.heb:
*צֹר.* 
לְשׁוֹן צוּר.
rashi.eng: *rock.* Heb. צֹר, an expression of צוּר, a rock.

rashi.heb:
*מֵחֶבֶל אַכְזִיבָה.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) מֵעֲדַב אַכְזִיבָה, מִגּוֹרָל כְּזִיב.
rashi.eng: *from the lot of Achzib.* lit from the rope of Achzib, from the lot of Chezib.

notes.690: (tn): The words “in all they had” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

notes.691: (tn, Heb): “this was the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Asher.”

notes.692: (tn, Heb): “the sixth lot came out for the sons of Naphtali, for the sons of Naphtali.”

notes.693: (tn, Heb): “and their border was from Heleph, from the oak of Zaanannim, and Adami Nekeb, and Jabneel to Lakkum.”
notes.694: (tn): The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied for clarity.

notes.695: (tc): The MT reads “Judah, the Jordan”; the LXX omits “Judah.” Perhaps there was a town named Judah, distinct from the tribe of Judah, located near the northern end of the Jordan.

rashi.heb:
*וְעָרֵי מִבְצָר.* 
הָיוּ לְנַפְתָּלִי הַצִּדִּים צֵר.
rashi.eng: *And the fortress cities.* which belonged to Naphtali were: Ziddim, Zer, etc.

notes.696: (map): For location see Map1-D2; Map2-D3; Map3-A2; Map4-C1.

notes.697: (sn): Instead of Yiron some English translations read Iron.
notes.698: (tn): The words “in all they had” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

notes.699: (tn, Heb): “this was the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali.”

notes.700: (tn, Heb): “the seventh lot came out for the sons of Dan.”

rashi.heb:
*צָרְעָה וְאֶשְׁתָּאוֹל.* 
מִשֶּׁל יְהוּדָה הָיָה (לעיל טו לג), וְנָפַל גּוֹרָל בְּנֵי דָּן סָמוּךְ לָהֶם.
rashi.eng: *Zorah, and Eshtaol.* They belonged to Judah, and the lot of the children of Dan fell adjacent to them.

notes.701: (tn, Heb): “the territory of the sons of Dan went out from them.”
notes.702: (tn, Heb): “Leshem.” The pronoun (“it”) has replaced the name “Leshem” in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.703: (tn, Heb): “according to the name of their father.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיֵּצֵא גְּבוּל בְּנֵי־דָן־מֵהֶם.* 
כָּאן נָטְלוּ קְצָת וְעוֹד נָפַל לָהֶם גּוֹרָל בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר רָחוֹק מִגְּבוּלָם, וּשְׁאָר שְׁבָטִים מַפְסִיקִין בֵּינְתַיִם.
rashi.eng: *And the border of the children of Dan went out from them.* The children of Dan took part [of their inheritance] here, and they also received a lot elsewhere far from their border, with the other tribes intervening between them.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּלָּחֲמוּ עִם לֶשֶׁם.* 
לְאַחַר זְמַן בִּימֵי עָתְנִיאֵל בֶּן קְנַז, וּבִימֵי פֶּסֶל מִיכָה, כְּמָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּסֵפֶר שׁוֹפְטִים (יח ב).
rashi.eng: *and fought against Leshem.* at a later time, in the days of Othniel the son of Kenaz and in the days of Micah’s graven image, as is stated in the book of Judges.

rashi.heb:
*לֶשֶׁם.* 
הִיא לַיִשׁ הָאֲמוּרָה בְּסֵפֶר שׁוֹפְטִים (יח יד).
rashi.eng: *Leshem.* identical with Laish mentioned in the Book of Judges.

notes.704: (tn, Heb): “this was the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Dan.”

notes.706: (tn, Heb): “the leaders of the fathers of the tribes.”
notes.707: (tn, Heb): “at the entrance of the tent of assembly.” On the tent of meeting see Exod 33:7-11.

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר נָחֲלוּ.* 
הִנְחִילוּ.
rashi.eng: *divided for an inheritance.* lit., caused to inherit.

notes.708: (tn, Heb): “Say to the sons of Israel, ‘Set aside for yourselves.’”

notes.710: (tn, Heb): “so that the one who kills, taking life accidentally without knowledge, may flee there.”

notes.711: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the one who accidentally kills another, cf. v. 2) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.712: (tn, Heb): “and speak into the ears of the elders of that city his words.”
notes.713: (tn, Heb): “and they should gather him into the city to themselves, give to him a place, and he will live with them.”

notes.714: (tn, Heb): “for without knowledge he killed his neighbor, and he was not hating him prior to that.”

notes.716: (tn, Heb): “until he stands before the assembly for judgment.”
notes.717: (tn, Heb): “until the death of the high priest who is in those days.”
notes.718: (tn, Heb): “may return and enter his city and his house, the city from which he escaped.”

rashi.heb:
*עַד עָמְדוֹ וְגוֹ' לַמִּשְׁפָּט.* 
אִם יִפָּטֵר מִגָּלוּת יִפָּטֵר, וְאִם יִתְחַיֵּיב גָּלוּת יַחֲזוֹר לְעִיר מִקְלָטוֹ (במדבר לה נה): וְיֵשֵׁב שָׁם עַד מוֹת הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל.
rashi.eng: *until he stand before the tribunal for judgment.* If he be freed from exile he is dismissed. If, however, he is sentenced to exile, he is remanded to his refuge city, where he must dwell until the death of the High Priest.

notes.720: (map): For the location of Jericho see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

rashi.heb:
*וּמֵעֵבֶר לְיַרְדֵּן יְרִיחוֹ מִזְרָחָה נָתְנוּ.* 
בִּימֵי משֶׁה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דברים ד מג): אֶת בֶּצֶר בַּמִּדְבָּר וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *And of the other side of the Jordan at Jericho eastward, they had assigned.* during Moses’ time as it is stated: Bezer in the wilderness, etc.

notes.722: (tn): The Hebrew text reads simply “the cities.” The words “for refuge” are supplied for clarification.
notes.723: (tn, Heb): “and not die by the hand of.”
notes.724: (tn, Heb): “until he stands before the assembly.” The words “at least” are supplied for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*הַמּוּעָדָה.* 
הַהַזְמָנָה הַיְעוּדוֹת לְכָךְ.
rashi.eng: *set apart.* lit., the cities of setting apart, those set apart for this.

rashi.heb:
*וְלִבְנֵי קְהָת הַנּוֹתָרִים.* 
הֵם בְּנֵי משֶׁה וּבְנֵי יִצְהָר וְחֶבְרוֹן וְעֻזִּיאֵל.
rashi.eng: *And the rest of the children of Kohath.* They are the children of Moses, and the children of Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel.

rashi.heb:
*מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת מַטֵּה אֶפְרַיִם.* 
מִנַּחֲלַת שֵׁבֶט בְּנֵי אֶפְרַיִם נָפְלוּ לָהֶם אֵלֶּה הֶעָרִים, שֶׁבְּכָל שֵׁבֶט וְשֵׁבֶט נָטְלוּ, כְּמָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (במדבר לה ח): מֵאֵת הָרַב תַּרְבּוּ וּמֵאֵת הַמְּעַט תַּמְעִיטוּ אִישׁ כְּפִי נַחֲלָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר יִנְחָלוּ יִתֵּן מֵעָרָיו לַלְוִיִּם.
rashi.eng: *from the families of the tribe of Ephraim.* These cities fell to them from the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Ephraim, for they received cities in the inheritance of each tribe, as it is stated: “From the many you shall take many, and from the few you shall take few; each tribe according to its inheritance which they inherit, shall give of its cities to the Levites.”

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָא אֶתְהֶן בְּשֵׁם.* 
לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הִזְכִּיר לְמַעְלָה אֶת שְׁמוֹת הֶעָרִים שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ לָהֶם, וּלְמַטָּה הוּא מְפָרֵשׁ אֶת שְׁמוֹתָם, לְכָךְ אָמַר: אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָא אֶתְהֶן בְּשֵׁם.
rashi.eng: *these cities that will be mentioned by name.* Since above he did not mention the names of the cities which they gave them, and below he enumerates them, he, therefore, states: These cities that will be mentioned by name.

notes.726: (tn, Heb): “and it belonged to the sons of Aaron, from the Kohathite clans, from the sons of Levi.”

notes.727: (tn): The words “they assigned” are supplied for clarification (also in vv. 23, 25).

rashi.heb:
*וְאֶת עַלְמוֹן.* 
וּבְדִבְרֵי הַיָּמִים (דברי הימים א ו מה): וְאֶת עָלֶמֶת, הִיא בַּחוּרִים, שֶׁיּוֹנָתָן (שמואל ב ג טז) מְתַרְגֵּם אוֹתָהּ: עֲלָמוֹת.
rashi.eng: *And 'Almon.* and in Chron.: “and 'Alemeth.” That is Bahurim which Jonathan renders: עַלְמוֹת

notes.728: (tn): The name “Gath Rimmon” is problematic here, for it appears in the preceding list of Danite cities. The LXX reads “Iebatha”; 1 Chr 6:55 HT (6:70 ET) reads “Bileam.” Most modern translations retain the name “Gath Rimmon,” however.

notes.729: (tn): The words “they assigned” and “the following cities” are supplied for clarification (also in v. 34).

notes.730: (tc): are accidentally omitted from a number of significant Hebrew mss. They are, however, found in some Hebrew mss, the LXX and Vulgate.

rashi.heb:
*אֶת מִגְרָשֶׁיהָ סְבִיבוֹתֶיהָ.* 
אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכָל רוּחַ.
rashi.eng: *and its open land around.* two thousand ells on each side.

notes.731: (tn, Heb): “in the midst of the possession of the sons of Israel.”

notes.732: (tn, Heb): “these cities were city [by] city, and its grazing areas [were] around it; so [it was] for all these cities.”

notes.733: (tn, Heb): “which he had sworn to give to their fathers.”

notes.736: (tn, Heb): “according to all he swore to their fathers.”
notes.737: (tn, Heb): “not a man stood from before them from all their enemies.”

notes.738: (tn, Heb): “the house of Israel.” Cf. NCV “the Israelites”; TEV “the people of Israel”; CEV, NLT “Israel.”
notes.739: (tn, Heb): “not a word from all the good word which the Lord spoke to the house of Israel fell; the whole came to pass.”

notes.740: (tn, Heb): “You have kept all which Moses, the Lord’s servant, commanded you, and you have listened to my voice, to all which I commanded you.”

notes.741: (tn, Heb): “your brothers” (also in vv. 4, 7), but this does not refer to siblings or necessarily even to relatives. It refers to the Israelites of the remaining tribes.
notes.743: (tn, Heb): “you have kept the charge of the command of the Lord your God.”

notes.744: (tn, Heb): “has given rest to your brothers.”

notes.747: (tn, Heb): “But be very careful to do the commandment and the law which Moses, the Lord’s servant, commanded you, to love.”

notes.752: (tn, Heb): “blessed.” However, see v. 8, where rewards are given.
notes.753: (tn, Heb): “and they went to their tents.”

rashi.heb:
*וְגַם כִּי שִׁלְּחָם יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.* 
לַחֲצִי שֵׁבֶט הַמְנַשֶּׁה, כַּאֲשֶׁר שָׁלַח אֶת בְּנֵי רְאוּבֵן וְגָד.
rashi.eng: *And also when Joshua sent them away.* i.e., the half tribe of Manasseh, as he had sent away the children of Reuben and Gad.

rashi.heb:
*עִם אֲחֵיכֶם.* 
בְּנֵי רְאוּבֵן וּבְנֵי גָּד, וְיֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִין: עִם אֲחֵיכֶם שֶׁנִּשְׁאֲרוּ לִשְׁמוֹר אֶת הֶעָרִים עִם הַנָּשִׁים וְהַטַּף, וְלֹא עָבְרוּ אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן עִם הַחֲלוּצִים, גַּם הֵם נָטְלוּ חֵלֶק בַּבִּזָּה.
rashi.eng: *divide the spoil… with your brothers.* the children of Reuben and the children of Gad. Some interpret this to mean: With your brothers who remained to guard the cities with the women and children, and did not cross the Jordan with the advance guard. They too received a share of the spoils.

rashi.heb:
*לַעֲלוֹת עֲלֵיהֶם לַצָּבָא.* 
לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֶסְרוּ הַבָּמוֹת מִשֶּׁנִּקְבַּע הַמִּשְׁכָּן בְּשִׁילֹה.
rashi.eng: *to go up to war against them.* For high places had been banned since the establishment of the tabernacle at Shiloh.

notes.764: (tn, Heb): “ten leaders with him, one leader, one leader for a paternal house, for all the tribes of Israel, and each a head of the house of their father, they belong to the clans of Israel.”

notes.765: (tn, Heb): “What is this unfaithfulness with which you have been unfaithful against the God of Israel, turning today from after the Lord, when you built for yourselves an altar, rebelling today against the Lord?”

notes.770: (sn): The western tribes here imagine a possible motive for the action of the eastern tribes. T. C. Butler explains the significance of the land’s “impurity”: “East Jordan is impure because it is not Yahweh’s possession. Rather it is simply ‘your possession.’ That means it is land where Yahweh does not live, land which his presence has not sanctified and purified” (Joshua [WBC], 247).

rashi.heb:
*אִם טְמֵאָה אֶרֶץ אֲחֻזַּתְכֶם.* 
שֶׁלֹּא בָּחַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַשְׁרוֹת בָּהּ שְׁכִינָתוֹ.
rashi.eng: *if the land of your possession is unclean.* For the Holy One, Blessed be He, did not choose it to cause His presence to rest therein.

rashi.heb:
*וְאֹתָנוּ אַל תִּמְרֹדוּ.* 
כְּמוֹ: וּבָנוּ אַל תִּמְרוֹדוּ.
rashi.eng: *nor rebel against us.* Heb. וְאוֹתָנוּ, instead of תִּמְרֹדוּ וּבָנוּ אַל.

notes.775: (tn, Heb): “Is it not [true that] Achan son of Zerah was unfaithful with unfaithfulness concerning what was set apart [to the Lord] and against all the assembly of Israel there was anger?”
notes.776: (tn): The second half of the verse reads literally, “and he [was] one man, he did not die for his sin.” There are at least two possible ways to explain this statement: (1) One might interpret the statement to mean that Achan was not the only person who died for his sin. In this case it could be translated, “and he was not the only one to die because of his sin.” (2) Another option, the one reflected in the translation, is to take the words וְהוּא אִישׁ אֶחָד (v�hu’ ’ish ’ekhad, “and he [was] one man”) as a concessive clause and join it with what precedes. The remaining words (לֹא גָוַע בַּעֲוֹנוֹ, lo’ gava’ ba’avono) must then be taken as a rhetorical question (“Did he not die for his sin?”). Taking the last sentence as interrogative is consistent with the first part of the verse, a rhetorical question introduced with the interrogative particle. The present translation has converted these rhetorical questions into affirmative statements to bring out more clearly the points they are emphasizing. For further discussion, see T. C. Butler, Joshua (WBC), 240.

notes.777: (tn, Heb): “answered and spoke to the heads of.”

notes.778: (sn): Israel’s God is here identified with three names: (1) אֵל (’el), “El” (or “God”); (2) אֱלֹהִים (’elohim), “Elohim” (or “God”), and (3) יְהוָה (y�hvah), “Yahweh” (or “the Lord”). The name אֵל (’el, “El”) is often compounded with titles, for example, El Elyon, “God Most High.”

notes.781: (tn, Heb): “do not save us.” The verb form is singular, being addressed to either collective Israel or the Lord himself. The LXX translates in the third person.

rashi.heb:
*אֵל אֱלֹהִים ה'.* 
אֵל כָּל הָאֱלֹהִים הוּא ה' הַיּוֹדֵעַ כִּי לֹא בְּמֶרֶד וְגוֹמֵר, וּכְשֶׁכָּפַל לוֹמַר שְׁתֵּי פְּעָמִים אֱלֹהִים, בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וּבָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
rashi.eng: *God, God, the Lord.* God of all the divine creatures [angels], He is the Lord, who knows that not in rebellion nor in transgression, etc. The repetition of the Name of God [is for the purpose of proclaiming their belief in one God both] in this world and in the world to come.

rashi.heb:
*אַל תּוֹשִיעֵנוּ.* 
כְּלַפֵּי שְׁכִינָה אָמְרוּ.
rashi.eng: *save as not.* They directed this statement toward the Divine Presence.

rashi.heb:
*מִדְּאָגָה מִדָּבָר.* 
מֵחֲמַת דַּאֲגַת יִרְאַת דְּבַר חֶרְפָּה עָשִׂינוּ, כְּמָה שֶׁמְּפֹרָשׁ פֶּן יֹאמְרוּ בְּנֵיכֶם מָחָר לְחָרֵף אֶת בָּנֵינוּ, כְּשֶׁיֵּלְכוּ לְהַקְרִיב בְּמִשְכַּן שִׁילֹה, שֶׁמָּא יֹאמְרוּ מַה לָּכֶם וְלַה', וַהֲלֹא גְּבוּל נָתַן בֵּינֵינוּ וּבֵינֵיכֶם אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן, זוֹ דָּאַגְנוּ וְעָשִׂינוּ. כָּל 'דְּאָגָה' שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָא לְשׁוֹן יִרְאָה הוּא, כְּמוֹ (ירמיהו לח יט): אֲנִי דּוֹאֵג אֶת הַיְּהוּדִים, דְּצִדְקִיָּהוּ.
rashi.eng: *for fear of this thing.* Because of דְּאָגַת, i.e., the fear of insulting words we have done this, as the Scripture explains: Lest in time to come, your children say, to insult our children when they go to sacrifice in the Tabernacle of Shiloh, lest they say, ‘what have you to do with the Lord? Did he not place the Jordan between us and you as a border?’ We feared this, and made [the altar]. Every דְּאָגָה in the Scriptures is an expression of fear, e.g., “I fear the Jews (דֹּאֵג) of Zedekiah.”

*וְלִצְנִנִים.* 
לְשׁוֹן מַחֲנוֹת, וְכֵן (יחזקאל כג כד): וּבָאוּ עָלַיִךְ הֹצֶן, כְּצִנָּה זוֹ הַמַּקֶּפֶת אֶת הָאָדָם מִשָּׁלשׁ רוּחוֹת, כְּמָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (תהלים ה יג): כַּצִּנָּה רָצוֹן תַּעְטְרֶנּוּ תְּסוֹבְבֶנוּ, כְּמוֹ (שמואל א כג כו): וְשָׁאוּל וַאֲנָשָׁיו עֹטְרִים אֶל דָּוִד וְאֶל אֲנָשָׁיו, עֹטְרִים סוֹבְבִים.

notes.896: (sn): For an excellent discussion of Joshua’s logical argument here, see T. C. Butler, Joshua (WBC), 274-75.
notes.897: (tn): In the Hebrew text both the divine name (אֱלֹהִים, ’elohim) and the adjective (קְדֹשִׁים, q�doshim, “holy”) are plural. Normally the divine name, when referring to the one true God, takes singular modifiers, but this is a rare exception where the adjective agrees grammatically with the honorific plural noun. See GKC �124.i and IBHS 122.
notes.898: (tn, Heb): “lift up” or “take away.” This assertion obviously needs qualification, for the OT elsewhere affirms that God does forgive. Joshua is referring to the persistent national rebellion against the Mosaic covenant that eventually cause God to decree unconditionally the nation’s exile.

rashi.heb:
*אֱלֹהִים קְדוֹשִׁים.* 
בְּרוֹב מְקוֹמוֹת נִקְרָא כָּל לְשׁוֹן רַבָּנוּת לְשׁוֹן רַבִּים, כְּמוֹ (בראשית מב ל): אֲדֹנֵי הָאָרֶץ, (שם לט כ): אֲדֹנֵי יוֹסֵף, (שמות כב יד) : אִם בְּעָלָיו עִמּוֹ, (שמואל ב כ כג): אֲשֶׁר הָלְכוּ אֱלֹהִים לִפְדּוֹת, לְפִי שֶׁהַשֵּׁם הַזֶּה שֵׁם שְׂרָרָה הוּא.
rashi.eng: *a holy God.* Heb. אֱלֹהִים קְדֹשִים, a plural form. In most places, every expression of lordship appears in the plural form, like: “The lord of (אֲדוֹנֵי) the land”; “Joseph’s master (אֲדוֹנֵי)”, “if his master (בְּעָלָיו) is with him”; “that God (אֱלֹהִים) went (הָלְכוּ) to redeem,” because this name (אֱלֹהִים) is a name of majesty.

notes.901: (tn): The words “against you” are added for clarification.
notes.903: (tn, Heb): “after he did good for you.”

notes.904: (tn): The translation assumes that כִּי (ki) is emphatic. Another option is to take it as explanatory, “No, for we will….”

notes.906: (tn, Heb): “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen for yourselves the Lord to serve him.”
notes.907: (sn): Like witnesses in a court of law, Israel’s solemn vow to worship the Lord will testify against them in the divine court if the nation ever violates its commitment.

rashi.heb:
*עֵדִים אַתֶּם בָּכֶם.* 
רָאָה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שֶׁעֲתִידִין לְעַרְעֵר בִּימֵי יְחֶזְקֵאל וְלוֹמַר (יחזקאל כ לב): נִהְיֶה כַגּוֹיִם, לְפִיכָךְ הִכְבִּיד עֲלֵיהֶם עַכְשָׁיו, וּלְכָךְ הוּשַׁב לָהֶם בִּימֵי יְחֶזְקֵאל (שם פסוקים לב לג): וְהָעֹלָה עַל רוּחֲכֶם הָיֹה לֹא תִהְיֶה וְגוֹמֵר, חַי אֲנִי אִם לֹא בְיַד חֲזָקָה וְגוֹמֵר, כְּבָר קִבַּלְתֶּם עֲלֵיכֶם בִּימֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, וְלֹא תֹּאמְרוּ מַה שֶּׁקִּבַּלְנוּ עָלֵינוּ בִּימֵי משֶׁה כְּדֵי לִיכָּנֵס לָאָרֶץ עָשִׂינוּ, הֲרֵי בִּימֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כְּבָר נִכְנַסְתֶּם וְקִבַּלְתֶּם.
rashi.eng: *“You are witnesses against yourselves…”.* Joshua foresaw that they would contest [this covenant] in the days of Ezekiel, and say, “Let us be like the nations.” Therefore, he made it more difficult now. He therefore, answered them in the days of Ezekiel, “And that which enters your thoughts, shall not come to pass, etc. As I live, etc., surely with a strong hand, etc.” You have already accepted upon yourselves in the days of Joshua. And you shall not say, “The covenant which we accepted upon ourselves in the days of Moses, we did only in order to enter the Land,” for in the days of Joshua you had already entered and you [nevertheless] accepted [the covenant].

notes.908: (tn): The words “Joshua said” are supplied for clarification.
notes.909: (tn, Heb): “bend your heart toward.” The term לֵבָב (levav, “heart”) probably here refers to the people’s volition or will.

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּשֶׂם לוֹ חֹק וּמִשְׁפָּט בִּשְׁכֶם.* 
סִידֵּר לָהֶם שָׁם הַחֻקִּים שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה וְקִבְּלוּ עֲלֵיהֶם.
rashi.eng: *and set them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem.* He arranged for them there, the statutes of the Torah, and they accepted them upon themselves.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּכְתֹּב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְגוֹמֵר.* 
תַּרְגּוּם יוֹנָתָן: וְכָתַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ יַת פִּתְגָּמַיָּא הָאִלֵּין וְאַצְנְעִינוּן בְּסֵפֶר אוֹרָיְיתָא דַה', וּבְמַסֶּכֶת מַכּוֹת (יא א) נֶחְלְקוּ אֲמוֹרָאִים: חַד אָמַר אֵלּוּ שְׁמוֹנָה פְּסוּקִים (דברים לד ה-יב) מִן 'וַיָּמֹת משֶׁה' עַד 'לְעֵינֵי כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל', שֶׁהֲרֵי סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה חָסֵר וְהִשְׁלִימוֹ, וְחַד אָמַר פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ שֶׁל עָרֵי מִקְלָט כָּתַב בְּסִפְרוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ כְּתוּבִים בְּסֵפֶר הַתּוֹרָה.
rashi.eng: *And Joshua wrote, etc..* Jonathan renders: And Joshua wrote these words and placed them in the Book of the Law of God. In the Tractate Makkoth, however, there is a divergence of opinion between two Amoraim. One says: These are the eight verses from: “And Moses died there,” until: “To the eyes of all Israel,”; for the scroll of the Law was incomplete, and he completed it. The other one says: This chapter of refuge cities he wrote in his Book, as they were written in the Book of the Law.

rashi.heb:
*תַּחַת הָאַלָּה.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) תְּחוֹת אַלְּתָא, הִיא מְזוּזוֹת הַפֶּתַח, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (מלכים א ו לא): הָאַיִל מְזוּזוֹת חֲמִשִׁית, וּמִדָּה אַחַת לָאֵלִים, וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים זוֹ הָאֵלָה אֲשֶׁר עִם שְׁכֶם, שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיַעֲקֹב (בראשית לה ד): וַיִּטְמֹן אֹתָם יַעֲקֹב תַּחַת הָאֵלָה.
rashi.eng: *under the doorpost.* Heb. הָאַלָּה תַּחַת. [Jonathan renders] תְּחוֹת אַלְתָא. This is the doorpost of the entrance, as it is stated: “The doorposts (האיל) having five angles, and one measure for the doorposts.” Others say that this was the oak near Shechem, about which it is written in connection with Jacob: “And Jacob hid them [the idols and their ornaments] under the oak (הָאֵלָה).”

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר בְּמִקְדַּשׁ ה'.* 
כְּלַפֵּי שֶׁהֵבִיאוּ שָׁם אֶת הָאֲרוֹן, כְּמָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לְמַעְלָה (פסוק א): וַיִּתְיַצְּבוּ לִפְנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים.
rashi.eng: *which is in the sanctuary of the Lord.* [This was not a permanent sanctuary, but it was called “the sanctuary of the Lord,”] because they brought the Ark there, as it is stated above: “And they presented themselves before God.”

notes.914: (tn, Heb): “all the words of the Lord which he spoke with us.”

rashi.heb:
*הָאֶבֶן הַזֹּאת תִּהְיֶה בָּנוּ לְעֵדָה וגו'.* 
(תַּרְגּוּם:) הָא אַבְנָא הָדָא תְּהֵי לָנָא כִּתְרֵין לוּחֵי אֶבֶן דִּקְיָימָה אֲרֵי יָתָהּ עֲבַדְנָא לְסַהֲדוּ אֲרֵי פִּתְגָּמַיָּא דִּכְתִיבִין עֲלָהּ מֵעֵין כָּל פִּתְגָמַיָא דַּה' דְּמַלֵיל עִמָּנָא. וְגַם יֵשׁ לְפוֹתְרוֹ כְּמַשְׁמָעוֹ, כִּי הִיא שָׁמְעָה אֶת הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתִּי לָכֶם בִּשְׁלִיחוּתוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם.
rashi.eng: *“Behold, this stone shall be a witness against us, etc.”.* Jonathan paraphrases: This stone shall be to us even as the two stone tablets of the covenant, for we have made it for a witness, for the words which are written thereon are similar to the words of the Lord which He spoke to us. We can also interpret this according to its simple meaning: for it has heard the words which I have spoken to you as a messenger of the Omnipresent.

notes.916: (tn, Heb): “And Joshua sent the people away, each to his inheritance.”

notes.918: (tn, Heb): “in the territory of his inheritance.”

rashi.heb:
*בְּתִמְנַת סֶרַח.* 
כָּךְ שְׁמָהּ, וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר (שופטים ב ט) הוּא קוֹרֵא אוֹתָהּ 'תִּמְנַת חֵרֶס', עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהֶעֱמִידוּ תְּמוּנַת הַחַמָּה עַל קִבְרוֹ (של יהושע), לוֹמַר זֶה הוּא שֶׁהֶעֱמִיד הַחַמָּה, וְכָל הָעוֹבֵר עָלֶיהָ אוֹמֵר חֲבָל עַל זֶה שֶׁעָשָׂה דָּבָר גָּדוֹל כָּזֶה וָמֵת. וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים, תִּמְנַת חֵרֶס שְׁמָהּ, וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמָהּ תִּמְנַת סֶרַח, עַל שֵׁם שֶׁפֵּירוֹתֶיהָ מַסְרִיחִין מֵרוֹב שֻׁמָּנַן.
rashi.eng: *in Timnath-serah.* So was its name. Elsewhere the Scripture calls is Timnath heres, because they set up a figure of the sun upon his grave. [חֶרֶס means sun, as in Jud. 8:13, 14:18, Job 9:7.] I.e., this is the one who caused the sun to stand still. And anyone who passes by it, says, "Woe to this one who performed such a great feat and died." Others say: its name was Timnath-heres, and why was it called Timnath-serah? Because its fruits would rot (מַסְרִיחִין) because of their great richness.

rashi.heb:
*לְהַר גָּעַשׁ.* 
מְלַמֵּד שֶׁרָעַשׁ עֲלֵיהֶם הָהָר לְהוֹרְגָם לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הִסְפִּידוּהוּ כָּרָאוּי.
rashi.eng: *of the hill of Gaash.* teaches us that the hill stormed forth (גָּעַשׁ) upon them to kill them, because they did not eulogize him properly.

notes.920: (tn, Heb): “all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who outlived him.”
notes.921: (tn, Heb): “who knew all the work of the Lord which he had done for Israel.”

rashi.heb:
*הֶאֱרִיכוּ יָמִים.* 
יָמִים הֶאֱרִיכוּ, שָׁנִים לֹא הֶאֱרִיכוּ, שֶׁנֶּעֶנְשׁוּ.
rashi.eng: *outlived.* הֶאֱרִיכוּ יָמִים. lit., Their days were lengthened but their years were not lengthened because they were punished.

notes.922: (tn, Heb): “one hundred qesitahs.” The Hebrew word קְשִׂיטָה (qesitah) is generally understood to refer to a unit of money, but the value and/or weight is unknown. The word occurs only here and in Gen 33:19 and Job 42:11.
notes.923: (tn, Heb): “and they became for the sons of Joseph an inheritance.” One might think “bones” is the subject of the verb “they became,” but the verb is masculine, while “bones” is feminine. The translation follows the emendation suggested in the BHS note, which appeals to the Syriac and Vulgate for support. The emended reading understands “the part (of the field)” as the subject of the verb “became.” The emended verb is feminine singular; this agrees with “the part” (of the field), which is feminine in Hebrew.

rashi.heb:
*קָבְרוּ בִּשְׁכֶם.* 
מִשְּׁכֶם גְּנָבוּהוּ, לִשְׁכֶם הֶחֱזִירוּהוּ.
rashi.eng: *they buried in Shechem.* From Shechem they kidnapped him; therefore to Shechem they returned him.

notes.924: (tn, Heb): “in Gibeah of Phinehas, his son, which had been given to him in the hill country of Ephraim.”

rashi.heb:
*בְּגִבְעַת פִּינְחָס בְּנוֹ.* 
מֵהֵיכָן הָיָה לוֹ לְפִינְחָס חֵלֶק בָּאָרֶץ, שֶׁיָּרַשׁ מֵאִשְׁתּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *in the hill of Phinehas his son.* Whence did Phinehas receive a part in the Land of Israel [if not from his father]? He inherited it from his wife.
